productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted a new laptop for personal use as well as mostly moderate gaming, and this laptop is great for all my purposes (i9, 32GB RAM, 1TB storage). I consider the price I paid ($1746) reasonable compared with similar laptops, but it does go on sale sometimes.The laptop is a little on the heavy and slightly bulky side for casual use, but I wouldn’t have minded if it was even bigger than it is if that meant better cooling, less cost, etc. It really not too bulky for a gaming laptop. Size aside, it looks great. Stylish and sleek, and the customizable and dimmable keyboard backlighting is a nice touch. I like the keyboard layout for typing as well as gaming, I find it to be very functional. The number pad is small but usable. The function keys are well thought out (function keys for screen brightness, keyboard backlighting brightness, enable/disable touchpad, mute mic, etc.), which I find to be rare with laptops. There’s a light for function lock and mic muting. WASD are a different color for gaming.The laptop runs Windows 11 well and seems very fast and powerful (although I haven’t done anything yet to truly push its limits). The BIOS is pretty reasonable, based on my experience (IT professional). The MSI app with designated function key lets you quickly change the power mode for your purposes, although my limited experience with the AI mode has not been great so far (it throttled the power down when I needed it, reasons unknown, and it turned off the keyboard backlighting at night). I’ve only played a few games on it so far, but it handles Fortnite like a champ without needing its full capabilities (power setting on “balanced” works perfectly). I haven’t run into any major issues with other programs or OS yet. Worth noting, the laptop does not always shut down properly. I’ve had to disable sleep and hibernation in Windows, as the laptop frequently does not resume from those states gracefully. Sometimes the laptop does not shut down completely at all, and the Embedded Controller keeps the fans running indefinitely, until I hold down the power button to manually power it off. That’s not ideal, but for me it’s not too big a deal either.The laptop also runs hot when in performance power mode or when gaming. I would never use a gaming laptop without a cooling pad, but if you’re new to gaming laptops, take note. The laptop seems to manage its built in fans well (and there’s a keyboard function key to let you immediately turn all the fans on to max speed), but again, I advise a cooling pad with fans to ensure you don’t overheat it during any use more intensive than watching videos. Definitely don’t ever put this down on a soft surface (like a bed or couch) without a hard flat surface under it or you’ll probably melt it.The power supply is bulky, as you would expect for a laptop that needs extra power for gaming, and the power supply also gets hot. Best to keep it where it can easily cool when in use. The power cord has a third prong/ground.All around, a great gaming laptop for a reasonable price.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolutely a beast for gaming, but loud on Fan Boost.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am a gamer that likes to play both modern and older games. The computer has no compatibility issues with older games so far, and runs all the modern games with no issues. I have it attached to an external 32" gaming monitor and play games like 7D2D on the highest settings. The screen is bright and the laptop hinges for the lid to the body seem well made.The battery life when playing heavy games last about 45 minutes, but lasts about an hour and a half when playing only music. I take the laptop with me everywhere I go. The sound quality is impressive and can get pretty loud, however it needs to be loud for my next point.The only negative feedback that I have is part of a double-edge sword. When doing normal activities, the laptop runs cool to warm. There is enough air speed in the fans to keep the laptop from getting real hot when heavily gaming, however you would need to use the Fan Boost to do that. The trade off is the sound from the fan sounds like a mattress air pump. It does push a LOT of air, so I guess there has to be a trade off.Would I buy this laptop again? Absolutely!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As someone who’s been building and using gaming PCs for years, I picked up the MSI Katana 15 HX B14WGK-016US primarily for portability without compromising performance—and I’m impressed with what this system delivers.First off, the Core i9-14900HX and RTX 5070 combo is no joke. This laptop chews through modern AAA titles without breaking a sweat. I’m seeing 100+ FPS on high to ultra settings in titles like Cyberpunk 2077, Hogwarts Legacy, and Call of Duty MW3, and it stays consistent even during long sessions. MSI did a solid job with thermals—kick on Cooler Boost and it stays cool enough without thermal throttling. The 165Hz display really helps the experience feel fluid in competitive titles.Stability is another strong point. No weird crashes, no blue screens, no random freezes—just reliable, smooth performance. And coming from a brand like MSI, that doesn’t surprise me. I’ve used their graphics cards and motherboards in my builds for years, and they’ve always delivered.  MSI overall I’ve had a good experience with their products That same engineering shows up in this laptop.That said, there are some things to be aware of. Battery life isn’t great—maybe 4 hours max under light use, and much less if you’re doing anything demanding. For some this laptop could be heavy for a 15-inch laptop, but others will say its not. I didn’t pick this laptop for its light weight design. It was about performance and portability. The chassis is plastic but metal feel and pretty basic clean design, though it feels solid enough. The RGB keyboard looks great, but the number pad layout is cramped and takes getting used to.Out of the box, expect sometime to setup— Windows updates, and drivers, etc.Bottom line: if you’re a gamer who prioritizes performance and value, this is a fantastic machine for the price. You’re getting high-end GPU and CPU power without paying $2K+. It's not a luxury laptop—it’s a focused, performance-driven tool for gaming and heavy workloads. Highly recommend for experienced users who want desktop-like power in a mobile form.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to replace a 6 year old Eluktronics laptop.  Worked perfect until it kept crashing multiple times per day for no reason.  After doing a lot of research, this seemed like a solid choice for a gaming laptop.  Not high end super-duper intensive gaming, but it works for my gaming needs.Obviously, like most new computers, set-up can be tedious, and some people may try to rush the process.  My suggestion is to let Windows do ALL of their updates before you start installing your apps.  Let your other onboard hardware do the same.  Then, after everyone is all happy and up-to-date, you can install your stuff.  It went error-free for me.  After a few days of additional tweaking, I got this new laptop to "feel" like the workhorse it replaced.  Plus, I have the reassurance that I should get several years of dependable service.Now, the unhappy discoveries that I made:1.  The built in webcam is not "Windows Hello" compatible.  I hadn't really thought about this ahead of time.  My OLD laptop's built-in camera worked just fine with Hello.  I got used to using this login feature.  I miss this feature.2.  There really aren't enough USB ports.  I am now using 3 of 4 ports.  One is for a fingerprint device (see above complaint).  It would be a cool feature if a corner of the built-in mouse pad had fingerprint technology...  Another port is being used for a laptop cooling riser.  Yes, this laptop has pretty good cooling, but adding more comes in handy with heavy usage.  The 3rd port in use is for a portable hard drive.  This leaves 1 port for available use.All in all, it's a really affordable laptop for better-than-just-basic gaming as well as general duty use for everything else.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
A new age of power is born 

Experience Alienware's flagship 16-inch gaming laptop, built with innovation that brings performance to the most passionate. 
16.0" WQXGA (2560x1600) 240Hz 3ms 100% DCI-P3 500 nit, ComfortView+, NVIDIA G-SYNC+, FHD Camera Advanced Optimus Display
Intel Core Ultra 9 processor 275HX (24-Core, 36MB Total Cache, 2.7GHz to 5.4GHz)
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12GB GDDR7 Graphics Card
1TB NVMe M.2 PCIe Gen4 SSD
32GB, 2x16GB, DDR5, 6400MT/s Memory

aplus content video
Playtime. Anytime. 

Play the latest games with graphics that rival reality. Play with players on console. Play with the peripherals that you love. When it comes to playing your way, Windows 11 makes it happen. 
The new performance precedent 

Alienware Area-51 gaming laptops are engineered for maximum power, packed with innovation, and encased in otherworldly design. By fusing an advanced thermal strategy, increasing airflow and elevating power with Intel Core Ultra HX processors and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptop GPUs, we're bringing alien-class performance to the most passionate gamers. 
Unapologetic power 

Area-51 was intentionally designed to reach new performance horizons by enabling higher graphics and processor power limits. With more power provided to the silicon components, gamers can run their games on the highest settings, making this our most powerful 16" gaming laptop yet. 
Up to 65W: CPU Thermal Design Power means full power devoted towards processing tasks in real-time. 
Based on internal Dell analysis, December 2024. 
Game changing graphics 

Step into the future of gaming and creation with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptop GPUs, powered by NVIDIA Blackwell and AI. Designed to push boundaries, RTX 50 Series with NVIDIA Max-Q delivers optimized battery life and performance and jaw-dropping graphics fidelity—perfect for those who demand the extraordinary on the go. 
Ray Tracing Redefined: Experience cinematic realism with full ray tracing. 
AI-Boosted Gameplay: Unleash next-level performance and image quality with DLSS 4. 
Intelligent processing 

Intel Core Ultra HX processors integrate CPU, built-in GPU, and NPU into a single package designed for AI acceleration and balanced performance across your favorite things to do. 
CPU: Ensures everything runs smoothly and as expected; like controlling non-player characters. 
NPU: Uses AI with compatible livestreaming software to remove your background thus offloading this performance demand from the CPU or GPU. 
iGPU: Delivers graphics rendering capabilities and imagery editing power at home. 
Supercharged data stream 

Multitasking for Gamers and Creators: With two SO-DIMM slots designated for DDR5 system memory, Area-51 laptops can support up to 64GB of memory. 
Subject to third party purchase of additional memory. 
Introducing the Cryo-Chamber 

Developed by our engineers, Area-51’s new Cryo-Chamber structure, located at the bottom of the laptop, focuses air to the core components where it matters the most. The Cryo-Chamber props up the laptop and introduces a much larger air intake, promoting increased airflow, and features a clear Gorilla Glass panel providing a view of the AlienFX fans. 
Gorilla Glass panels on the Cryo-Chamber require a configuration with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti or higher. 
The video showcases the product in use.The video guides you through product setup.The video compares multiple products.The video shows the product being unpacked.
aplus content video
Performance Driven Thermals 

Marathon gaming requires absolute power. Our advanced cooling technology, Alienware Cryo-tech, is designed to maintain system stability even during the most demanding sessions. 
Quad fans 

Helps increase total airflow and pressurizes the chassis, keeping even the most aggressive hotspots properly cooled. 
Available on configurations with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and above. 
More copper, less heat 

With up to 3x more copper in weight than previous 16" laptops and a vapor chamber 40% larger, Alienware 16 Area-51 dynamically balances heat across up to 7 heat pipes making it our most performance forward 16" laptop to date. 
Based on internal Dell analysis, December 2024. 
Element 31 thermal interface 

Encapsulated gallium-silicone across the CPU, dissipates heat faster, allowing you to take on marathon gaming sessions with ease. 
The video showcases the product in use.The video guides you through product setup.The video compares multiple products.The video shows the product being unpacked.
aplus content video
Advanced dynamic lighting 

Ambient AlienFX lighting inspired by the aurora borealis takes on color and movement which reflects across surfaces to create an otherworldly experience. The masterful layering of materials marks a new level of technical ability and design sophistication. 
Zero hinge innovation 

A more robust closure and nearly invisible hinge creates a floating display. Engineered for strength and sophistication this patent pending design drives motion in the radial direction and telescopes out, enabling an adaptive rear design that features translucent materials and new AlienFX lighting. 
The video showcases the product in use.The video guides you through product setup.The video compares multiple products.The video shows the product being unpacked.
aplus content video
Bringing comfort to the forefront 

Our new Area-51 laptops combine mystery and otherworldly design with fluid contours and soft surfaces that inspires comfortable gameplay for hours. 
Contours: Fluid design contours with thoughtful edges provide enhanced tactile feeling. 
V-Rail edges: Easy and comfortable open and closing for the lid of your laptop. 
Pillowed palm rest: Seamless pillowed palm rest redefines comfort during any gaming session. 
Next-gen hardware in every aspect 

Incredible Battery: A larger 96WHr Lithium Ion battery enables fast charging and uses Alienware Battery Defender technology to optimize power consumption. 
Powerful Webcam: A new 8MP 4K HDR webcam delivers incredible resolution and clarity. 
Superior Wi-Fi: Area-51 laptops come standard with Wi-Fi 7 technology ensuring high peak rates and low latency across multiple connections. 
Versatile Thunderbolt: New Thunderbolt 5 technology provides the best connectivity to all your external devices. 
Total Command 

Control more than ever with Alienware Command Center. 
Convenient presets: Maximize your gameplay with performance presets for the power you need. 
Performance overlay: Manage and see CPU, GPU, memory and thermals stats without exiting the game. 
AlienFX: Customize your set up with lighting settings that extend to all your Alienware accessories. 
AlienVision: Toggle external Alienware monitor hardware-based overlays on/off to help you focus on the targets at hand. 
Windows Copilot Key 

With one click, you have instant access to Copilot in Windows – Your own personal AI assistant. Get real answers, inspiration and solutions at your fingertips. 
Copilot in Windows availability depends on local government regulation. For regions where Copilot is not available, pressing the Copilot key will bring up the Windows search menu.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Alienware seems to really gotten their act together recently. This laptop is beautiful, has a great high-quality feel to all the materials including the keyboard, and yet it’s actually a pretty good value given the performance specs. The only thing I can possibly complain about is the screen isn’t the highest quality. It’s got great frame rate, and nice color, but the contrast isn’t great, and the uniformity of blacks is pretty poor. I really wish Alienware would offer an OLED screen on what is supposed to be their flagship laptop, but that’s only a minor complaint. I’d certainly be happy to pay more to get a better screen, but at this price point the screen quality is acceptable.The thermals are much improved over the prior generation. There’s only so much they can do because they insist on using Intel processors, but they’ve done a nice job with the cooling on this one. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I took the week off work to play AAA games
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If it wasn't for the RGB lighting (and power brick), this would be an absolute sleeper-build of a laptop. 16", thin for a gaming laptop and lightweight. It fits my travel bags and looks like it belongs in an office environment. It's been a long time since I've had a reasonably sized laptop that was this powerful. The MSI software suit makes adjusting lighting easy and watching the internal temps puts my mind to ease. The triple fan system does a great job of keeping the laptop running without cooking itself. The screen is beautiful and is adequate for gaming. I don't feel like I'm missing anything from my bigger external monitors when I'm just on the laptop.Battery life is short, but that's to be expected on a power-hungry rig. I haven't timed it, but it seems like about 90 minutes is about norm with the power settings maxed.  When I run CAD and pull back the screen brightness and performance, I definitely saw longer times. The power brick is large and uses a propriety plug. I wish the power port was on the rear of the laptop instead of the left side. The plug has a locking function and doesn't pull out without a concerted effort; this is no magsafe adapter so protect your port. Supposedly I can power this with a 100W PD USB C power supply for basic (non-gaming) usage. All my USB C power supplies are only 65W so I can't test this, but it would be handy if I found my stranded without the dedicated brick.I was immediately able to pop in another SDD as the computer has one free slot. To upgrade the RAM, you'll have to replace one of the two RAM sticks already in the computer as there isn't any available slots.I was able to download a dozen AAA games from steam and get playing within an afternoon. I ran Battlefield 6 at max and didn't experience any lag, the laptop ran like it was built for these games. Solidworks works smoothly and my render times were pretty snappy for the parts I've been working on. I've also has Adobe Illustrator open at the same time without taxing the system. I've installed photo editing software, but haven't been able to pull myself away from gaming to do any photo editing yet. The real test is Microsoft Teams. That's always been a succabus of computer resources. Again, I'm doing too much gaming to return to office software. I'd expect I could run a video conference and CAD at the same time without crashing on this machine.Speedtests show 800Mbps download speeds on WIFI. I have both WIFI6 and 7 routers in my mesh network and I cannot tell a difference between them. I've tried to determine whether this laptop has a 6Ghz radio in it and I don't have an answer. Even my one year old flagship cell phone doesn't have a 6Ghz radio so I have trouble confirming performance there.The biggest thing I do not like on this laptop (besides the power brick which cannot be avoided) is the touchpad. It stops recognizing my finger if I hold it on the pad for a long time and the right click region is difficult for me to hit. When I game, I'm always using an external mouse so it's not a huge downer for me. The other thing is that I'm a big guy and the keyboard feels a bit cramped, even when gaming. The touchpad is well out of the way for the WASD keys so there is a solid wrist rest which I appreciate. As I type out this review, I have to pause to let feeling come back into my hands as it's difficult to bring my hands this close together to type. It's not a word processor, so that's okay. When docked at home, I have a mechanical keyboard which my body is accustomed to using.I'm not a serious gamer, I usually don't buy a title until a decade after it's been released. I've done this to be able to enjoy AAA titles at used game prices and let the hardware outpace the software needs. This is the first time I'm running a top of the line system and I think I'm unfortunately hooked. Come on GTA6...

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: There is no good use case for this computer :/
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm going to break this review down into categories and the follow it with my personal "using it like a laptop while traveling" experience coming up at the end. I apologize in advance that this will be a bit of a lengthy read, but I take computers very seriously and I really want this review to mean something, so I'm going to be completely honest about it.Performance:If raw performance is the only thing that mattered, this laptop would earn 5 stars. It's extremely powerful and posts great benchmarks, which you'd expect for the hardware that's in here.Screen Quality:The screen is fine. It's not OLED, which (given both the price and similarly priced and spec'd options from competitor brands) would have made far more sense, but it is still very smooth.Cooling:When you fit this much raw power into a relatively thin laptop, you have to find a way to keep it cool and that's certainly no easy task, but msi didn't rise to the challenge. Even when used on a flat desk in a cool room, this laptop runs HOT. And to be clear, this isn't limited to just super intensive gaming tasks; simply downloading and installing games from Steam will see this absolute beast BLASTING out 100 degree Fahrenheit air (a whopping 40 degrees over ambient)!!! The keyboard is situated mere milimeters above the hottest components in the machine, causing parts of it to become uncomfortably warm. BUT THE BIGGEST COOLING SIN OF THEM ALL is the fact that the cold air intake is on the bottom of the laptop, meaning that if you set this on a couch, bed, or basically anything other than a flat solid surface, you will choke out the intake. msi knew this was a bad design, but rather than change it, added a half inch tall rubber foot across the entire back edge of the bottom to ensure that it didn't also choke itself out on hard surfaces.Battery Life:I tested battery under three separate workloads, all at 30% volume and 50% brightness, all started at 100% and considered complete when Windows forcibly shut the laptop down to prevent battery harm. For my "Light Load Testing" I had a single chrome tab open playing a long form youtube video -- The battery lasted two hours and ten minutes. For my "Gamers and Creators" (msi was proud enough of this marketing term to put it on the box for the laptop as well as the velcro strap of the power supply) I streamed myself playing minecraft (without shaders or anything too terribly intensive), and the laptop died after an hour and 18 minutes. For my "All Out" testing, I ran Forza Horizon 6 at max settings with RayTracing and a bluetooth controller: the laptop died after 52 minutes.Portability:If the battery life and cooling situations didn't make it obvious, there are too many trade-offs made to shove all this hardware into a laptop for me to do consider this anything more than pseudo-portable. It has the same sort of "from one desk near an outlet to another desk near an outlet" sort of portability that a sewing machine with a handle has.Value for Money:This is where it all breaks down for me.  Spec for spec, this thing is less powerful and have worse benchmarks than a 4 year old desktop with a Ryzen 9 7900X, 64GB of DDR5 6000 MT/s RAM, and an RTX 4080 -- which I can find on marketplaces for an average of $1,400 less than the $3,600 asking price of this laptop. "But that's not a fair comparison! Those are desktops!" Given that this thing barely registers as portable, it may as well be a desktop. But to really drive home my comparison: Let's say you bought that 4080 desktop instead of this laptop. With the remaining $1,400 from your budget, you could do all of the following: Get an msi MAG series OLED monitor ($800), Get a Logitech G512 X 98 keyboard ($100) and  G502 Hero mouse ($70), and an Elgato FaceCam 4k ($200), an Elgato Stream Deck Mini ($50) and an Elgato Wave Neo USB Microphone ($65)... This laptop just isn't a compelling value for the money.What I learned while traveling with it:The necessity for a flat surface is this things biggest weakness. If, instead of a half inch rubber foot on the bottom, msi had simply made the wedge thicker, they could have nearly doubled the size of the heatsinks for the GPU and CPU, which would have allowed them to seal the bottom, draw cold air in from the sides, and exhaust the hot air out the back. This improved airflow pattern and heat dissipation would doubtlessly make the keyboard more pleasant to use. The charging brick for this laptop is an absolutely massive 330 watt power adapter with a proprietary connector. I'd have liked to see a more universal USB-C Power Delivery system so a more portable charger could be substituted, but this one isn't actually msi's fault; the spec sheet for USB-C PD doesn't support more than 240 Watts of power delivery, so using this on even a top-spec USB-C charger would cut your available performance (you know; the thing you're paying $3,600 for) by roughly 30%.If I had to be gracious, I would say that maybe this laptop is useful for a professional travel vlogger. The type who already transports a checked bag full of camera equipment and, therefore, would consider the prerequisite lap desk and external keyboard and mouse they'd need to actually do any useful video editing from this while travelling as something other than a deal breaker. That's still though as most video editors don't need this sort of power unless they're working in RAW 12k.And you know, maybe that's you: maybe you're traveling with $40k worth of filming equipment so what's another $3,600 on a laptop. But this is isn't poised as an industry grade workstation for professionals. It's for marketed at "gamers and creators" but I would say missed it's mark by approximately a thousand dollars.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I could gush over this laptop for many pages, but I'll try to summarize the highlights below. Note that I uploaded a quick 80-second video that shows unboxing and performance. I used the laptop for 2 weeks (14 days) before writing this review so I could be confident before reviewing a laptop that represents quite an investment for most people.I'll start with gaming performance. It's amazing for a mobile device! I tested with James Bond 007: First Light since it's a beast to run and because it's from Amazon MGM Studios and I hoped to avoid a copyright strike with my review video.Performance: When plugged in I got about 55 fps during gameplay at full resolution and high settings. When on battery this dropped way down to 15 fps (same settings) which is typical on a laptop due to battery limitations.Battery: It drains quickly when gaming. The battery drained about 10% every 7 minutes. By my calculations, that gives you about an hour of use when pushing the laptop to its limits. Charging the battery by 76% (from 21% to 97%) took 5 hours.Compatibility: I had no trouble when running Windows setup, or Steam, or games. Zero freezes or blue screens. All the devices in Control Panel had proper drivers and I didn't have to fix any banged-out items. I did install the Nvidia app to get the latest video drivers and I wanted the fps overlay.Display: The screen is bright and crisp. The resolution is higher than most laptops, especially vertically, which I appreciate.Misc: There are two USB C ports plus two USB A ports, video, audio, and even an Ethernet port if you want to avoid Wi-Fi for speed reasons. The keyboard is solid to use and the LEDs are beautiful. Even the logo on the laptop's lid lights up, which is a nice flex.In summary, this is priced in line with other gaming laptops but has a solid build, lighting, and polish that is hard to beat. It runs about half the speed of my similarly-priced desktop gaming rig (5070ti vid card) but if you want portability then this is a fun, powerful option.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Powerful gaming laptop with high end specs: RTX5080, 32GB, 2TB, 8980HX 16c/32t
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up this laptop after recently selling my old gaming laptop and switching to a thin and light non-gaming laptop, figuring I’d only do gaming on my desktop, but quickly missed it.Construction wise, this new MSI is well made, I think the top lid is metal, but everything else I believe is plastic. It does keep it lighter, and the palm rest has a nice smooth finish that doesn’t really feel like plastic. When gaming, being plastic, the palm wrest does stay very cool. The keyboard also only gets slightly warm. The only downside is it does show your palm prints, but it’s easy to wipe off. The logo on the lid lights up with the RGB color.The keyboard is nice, with configurable RGB. I like that the WASD and arrow keys are transparent, so they stand out, especially when lit, but otherwise are more subtle than other gaming keyboards that mold them in another color. I really like that it has full arrow keys, instead of the more typical layout where the up and down are small keys fitting into the space of a single key. It has a small trackpad, which I generally don’t use, but it’s compact, and the trackpad is still centered, so I don’t mind.During a long gaming session on balanced settings, the fans are very reasonable, no headphones needed, the keyboard stays cool to the touch, with no issues, it’s very fast. Doing a timespy benchmark, I got 16017 on balanced, 17035 on extreme, and 18696 with apex mode turned on. The fan would get pretty loud on apex mode, would want headphones, but it does give a fairly noticeable bump in performance. This laptop lets you give full speced wattage to the CPU and GPU, something that not all laptops do for cooling and other reasons, so you can use all available performance.The screen is very nice, the 240Hz rate is great, higher than my desktop PC. In Windows settings it seems to be either 60 or 240, and no adaptive mode. My own wish would be for an automatic brightness control. The webcam is good, with a hardware shutter, and windows hello face recognition which I love.The speakers are just decent, not amazing, they are better when using the nahamic profiles, I put it into automatic mode.I like how easily upgradable it is, a single smaller panel on the bottom can be removed to give access to the two PCIe SSD slots (the 4.0 is used, 5.0 is free), the two memory slots, CMOS battery, and access to clean the fan. Just open it and hold the little button under the panel for 10 seconds. This is something it seems like laptop makers stopped doing in the early 2010’s, requiring you to instead pull off the entire bottom panel with tons of tiny little screws.It does come with a hefty 330w power brick, when not gaming you can use a smaller USB-C charger. You need a 100w charger to charge the laptop while it’s on, but my 65w and 20w chargers would charge it when the laptop is off. For battery life, generally I always run the laptop plugged in, and I set a max charge of 80% to preserve the battery. I did try unplugging it, when it’s at 70%, Windows shows an estimated 4 hours battery life remaining.The overall specs are great, the Ryzen 9 8940HX is a 16 core, 32 thread Zen 4 part, that is just over a year old. My other laptop has a newer Zen 5 based Ryzen 9 AI 365, but this MSI laptop almost matches it in single core, but multicore the MSI blows it away by more than 80% in heavy multi-core loads, mainly just giving up some efficiency, not really the goal on a gaming desktop replacement. You get a healthy 32 GB of RAM, and a large 2TB SSD. Mine has a Samsung MZVL22T0HDLB-00BT, which is basically the OEM version of the 980 Pro, and quality, top of the line PCI-e 4.0 drive with DRAM cache. The star is the RTX5080 mobile, pretty much the top of the line GPU you can get today, with 16GB of VRAM.Final point is the price, this isn’t cheap, but it is the going price with the current component prices. This laptop has a top of the line GPU, lots of RAM, and a very large, high end SSD, all things that are most heavily affected by the price increases.Overall I’m very happy with this laptop.

Product description
GreatPriceTech sells computers with custom/upgraded configurations to enhance system performance. If the computer has modifications as listed above, then the manufacturer box was opened by our highly skilled technicians for testing and inspection and to install the upgrades according to the specifications as advertised. Both the computers and components are brand new for the upgraded system. 
Configuration 	We offer all of the following configurations, if you cannot find the correct listing please check for other listings on our Store page. 	
Model Name 	OmniBook X 	
Form/Color 	Standard/Glacier Silver 	
Display 	17.3" IPS FHD (1920x1080) 60Hz 16:9 Touchscreen Display 	
RAM 	32GB OnBoard LPDDR5X RAM 	
Hard Drive 	Customizable Storage: 2TB PCIe SSD, 4TB PCIe SSD, 8TB PCIe SSD (Solid State Drive) 	
Operating System 	Window 11 Professional (Win 11 Pro-64), Window 11 Home-64 	
Processor 	Intel Ultra 7-258V 2.20GHz Processor (15th Gen, upto 4.8 GHz, 12MB Cache, 8-Cores, 8-Threads, 4 Performance-cores) 	
Graphics Card 	Intel Arc 140V Integrated Graphics 	
Connectivity 	Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 	
Ports/Slots 	3 x USB 3.2 (Type-A), 1 x USB 3.2 (Type-C), 1 x HDMI, 1 x Thunderbolt and Headphone/Microphone Combo Jack 	
Other Features 	Grey Backlit Standard Keyboard, Webcam 	
Battery 	65W PSU, Type-C Power-In, 6-Cell 83 WHr Battery 	
Product Dimensions (WxLxH) 	10.25 IN x 15 IN x 0.9 IN 	
Weight 	5.5lb 	
Dockztorm 	Includes Authorized Dockztorm Portable USB Hub(Special Edition Portable Dockztorm Data Hub;Super Speedy Data Sync Rate upto 5Gbps) 	
Business Laptop 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop provides the ultimate experience for life and works anywhere. The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop is built with impressive reliability and robust security features. This device confidently handles whatever jobs come your way. Enjoy a more natural and comfortable typing position with the lift-hinge design and an enlarged clickpad. 
Processor and Graphics 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop is equipped with an Intel Ultra 7-258V 2.20GHz Processor (15th Gen, upto 4.8 GHz, 12MB Cache, 8-Cores, 8-Threads, 4 Performance-cores) and an Intel Arc 140V Integrated Graphics Card that provides smooth video for streaming, media editing, and more. 
Left Panel Ports 
The Left Panel of the HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop consists of 1 x USB 3.2 Type-A, 1 x USB 3.2 Type-C, 1 x HDMI and 1 x Thunderbolt 4 Ports. 
Right Panel Ports 
The Right Panel of the HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop consists of 2 x USB 3.2 Type-A port and Headphone/Microphone Jack Combo ports. 
IPS FHD Touch Display 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop supports a compact 17.3" Touchscreen IPS FHD Display, which brings big visuals with the Display panel, which lets you intuitively navigate and interact. With technology that lights each pixel separately, an IPS FHD Touchscreen display brings deeper blacks for richer contrast, enhanced color depth, and more power efficiency than traditional LED screens. A 17.3" Touchscreen IPS FHD Display delivers beautiful, brilliant colors, plus experience advanced power with a Intel Ultra Processor and impressive graphics. 
Powerful Performance 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop powers up the moment you open the lid and keeps your data safe wherever you’re working. Dynamic cooling manages the working temperature for optimum PC performance. Protect battery health and entertainment with automatic checks on battery temperature, charging status, and usage time. Designed to support higher data rates, address next-gen memory requirements, and have longer battery life. Multitask with ease thanks to the powerful Intel Ultra 7-258V 2.20GHz Processor. 
AI Copilot 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop features the innovative AI Copilot, a smart assistant designed to enhance your overall user experience. Leveraging artificial intelligence, the AI Copilot constantly analyzes your usage patterns to optimize performance, provide personalized recommendations, and automate routine tasks. It intelligently manages system resources, adjusts settings for improved efficiency, and even helps troubleshoot issues, ensuring your laptop runs smoothly and adapts to your workflow. 
Dockztorm Hub 
Authorized Dockztorm Portable USB Hub(Special Edition Portable Dockztorm Data Hub; Super Speedy Data Sync Rate up to 5Gbps). It is designed to be easily carried and suitable for on-the-go use, with a compact and lightweight form factor.

aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
GreatPriceTech sells computers with custom/upgraded configurations to enhance system performance. If the computer has modifications as listed above, then the manufacturer box was opened by our highly skilled technicians for testing and inspection and to install the upgrades according to the specifications as advertised. Both the computers and components are brand new for the upgraded system. 
Configuration 	We offer all of the following configurations, if you cannot find the correct listing please check for other listings on our Store page. 	
Model Name 	OmniBook X 	
Form/Color 	Standard/Glacier Silver 	
Display 	17.3" IPS FHD (1920x1080) 60Hz 16:9 Touchscreen Display 	
RAM 	32GB OnBoard LPDDR5X RAM 	
Hard Drive 	Customizable Storage: 2TB PCIe SSD, 4TB PCIe SSD, 8TB PCIe SSD (Solid State Drive) 	
Operating System 	Window 11 Professional (Win 11 Pro-64), Window 11 Home-64 	
Processor 	Intel Ultra 7-258V 2.20GHz Processor (15th Gen, upto 4.8 GHz, 12MB Cache, 8-Cores, 8-Threads, 4 Performance-cores) 	
Graphics Card 	Intel Arc 140V Integrated Graphics 	
Connectivity 	Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 	
Ports/Slots 	3 x USB 3.2 (Type-A), 1 x USB 3.2 (Type-C), 1 x HDMI, 1 x Thunderbolt and Headphone/Microphone Combo Jack 	
Other Features 	Grey Backlit Standard Keyboard, Webcam 	
Battery 	65W PSU, Type-C Power-In, 6-Cell 83 WHr Battery 	
Product Dimensions (WxLxH) 	10.25 IN x 15 IN x 0.9 IN 	
Weight 	5.5lb 	
Dockztorm 	Includes Authorized Dockztorm Portable USB Hub(Special Edition Portable Dockztorm Data Hub;Super Speedy Data Sync Rate upto 5Gbps) 	
Business Laptop 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop provides the ultimate experience for life and works anywhere. The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop is built with impressive reliability and robust security features. This device confidently handles whatever jobs come your way. Enjoy a more natural and comfortable typing position with the lift-hinge design and an enlarged clickpad. 
Processor and Graphics 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop is equipped with an Intel Ultra 7-258V 2.20GHz Processor (15th Gen, upto 4.8 GHz, 12MB Cache, 8-Cores, 8-Threads, 4 Performance-cores) and an Intel Arc 140V Integrated Graphics Card that provides smooth video for streaming, media editing, and more. 
Left Panel Ports 
The Left Panel of the HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop consists of 1 x USB 3.2 Type-A, 1 x USB 3.2 Type-C, 1 x HDMI and 1 x Thunderbolt 4 Ports. 
Right Panel Ports 
The Right Panel of the HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop consists of 2 x USB 3.2 Type-A port and Headphone/Microphone Jack Combo ports. 
IPS FHD Touch Display 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop supports a compact 17.3" Touchscreen IPS FHD Display, which brings big visuals with the Display panel, which lets you intuitively navigate and interact. With technology that lights each pixel separately, an IPS FHD Touchscreen display brings deeper blacks for richer contrast, enhanced color depth, and more power efficiency than traditional LED screens. A 17.3" Touchscreen IPS FHD Display delivers beautiful, brilliant colors, plus experience advanced power with a Intel Ultra Processor and impressive graphics. 
Powerful Performance 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop powers up the moment you open the lid and keeps your data safe wherever you’re working. Dynamic cooling manages the working temperature for optimum PC performance. Protect battery health and entertainment with automatic checks on battery temperature, charging status, and usage time. Designed to support higher data rates, address next-gen memory requirements, and have longer battery life. Multitask with ease thanks to the powerful Intel Ultra 7-258V 2.20GHz Processor. 
AI Copilot 
The HP OmniBook X AI Powered Laptop features the innovative AI Copilot, a smart assistant designed to enhance your overall user experience. Leveraging artificial intelligence, the AI Copilot constantly analyzes your usage patterns to optimize performance, provide personalized recommendations, and automate routine tasks. It intelligently manages system resources, adjusts settings for improved efficiency, and even helps troubleshoot issues, ensuring your laptop runs smoothly and adapts to your workflow. 
Dockztorm Hub 
Authorized Dockztorm Portable USB Hub(Special Edition Portable Dockztorm Data Hub; Super Speedy Data Sync Rate up to 5Gbps). It is designed to be easily carried and suitable for on-the-go use, with a compact and lightweight form factor.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is not a free review item for me. After thorough research and reading various bad reviews, with such a great price and extra software, I decided to invest in it, and I'm thrilled to share that it works exceptionally well! It arrived exactly as promised, with everything it was supposed to include.I did have to email them to obtain the Microsoft 365 key, but they responded swiftly within 24 hours~what great customer service! Personally, everything was flawless for me, and the setup was a breeze, including Microsoft 365 and pre-installed 11 Pro as advertised! The product itself has the right memory and specifications. I did notice the price changing multiple times. Mine, with a coupon at the time of purchase, was only $742.  I hope my experience can inform your decision-making. Just a friendly reminder... productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Alienware 18 Area-51 is an incredible machine. It feels less like a traditional laptop and more like a powerful desktop gaming PC that you can actually take with you.Performance is excellent. I play demanding games at maximum settings, and it handles them extremely well. The large 18-inch display makes gaming incredibly immersive, and everything feels smooth and responsive.One of the things that impressed me the most is the cooling system. It does an amazing job, and the Stealth Mode is fantastic. Even when playing demanding games at high settings, the laptop manages to stay surprisingly cool and quiet. I honestly didn’t expect a machine this powerful to handle heat and fan noise this well.The RGB lighting is absolutely top-notch and looks amazing, especially in the dark. The touchpad is another highlight — easily one of the coolest touchpads I’ve used on a gaming laptop.The only real downside is the size and weight. This thing is BIG and heavy. I actually had to buy a separate carrying case specifically for it. But honestly, considering the performance, huge screen, cooling system, and overall experience, I think it’s absolutely worth it.This is not a laptop for someone looking for maximum portability. But if you want a true desktop-replacement gaming machine that you can still take with you when needed, the Alienware 18 Area-51 is outstanding. I love it.

Who is the new Razer Blade 16 best suited for? 
The Blade 16 is ideal for competitive gamers, streamers, and creators who want flagship RTX 5090 performance in a thin, premium 16-inch gaming laptop. 
Is the new Razer Blade 16 good for gaming? 
Yes. The Razer Blade 16 is built for high-performance gaming with up to NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU and 165W TGP, delivering smooth frame rates in AAA titles and competitive esports games. 
What makes the new Razer Blade 16 different from other gaming laptops? 
It balances performance, display quality, portability, and premium build in one device rather than prioritizing only raw power or only portability. 
Should I choose Razer Blade 14, Blade 16, or Blade 18? 
The Blade 14 if you prioritize maximum portability. 
The Blade 16 if you want the best balance of performance, display immersion, and mobility. 
The Blade 18 if you want the largest display and closest-to-desktop experience. 
Is the Razer Blade 16 good for AI workloads? 
Yes. Powered by Intel Core Ultra 9 with up to 50 TOPS NPU performance and RTX 50 Series graphics, the Blade 16 supports AI-accelerated tasks such as content creation, rendering, and machine learning workflows.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using this MSI Cyborg 17 for both work and gaming, and it has exceeded my expectations.The 17.3-inch 144Hz display is smooth and immersive, making games look great while also providing plenty of screen space for productivity. The Intel Core 7 processor paired with the RTX 5060 handles everything I throw at it, from multitasking and content creation to modern AAA games with excellent performance.The 16GB DDR5 RAM and 1TB SSD make the system feel fast and responsive. Boot-up times are quick, applications load almost instantly, and there’s plenty of storage for games and files.I also appreciate the lightweight design for a 17-inch gaming laptop. The translucent black chassis gives it a unique futuristic look without being too flashy. Connectivity is solid with USB-C, Wi-Fi 6E, and enough ports for my accessories.The cooling system does a good job during long gaming sessions. The fans become noticeable under heavy load, but temperatures stay well under control, which is expected for a gaming laptop.Overall, this is an excellent value if you’re looking for a powerful gaming laptop that also works well for everyday use. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for strong performance, a large high-refresh-rate display, and modern hardware at a competitive price.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great laptop, could have been designed better
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Overall I'm happy with the laptop.  Let's start with the Cons.1) There is only 1 usb-c and 2 usb-a ports which is insufficient.2) The usb ports and the 3.5mm headset port are all positioned right on the right side where a right handed person would use a mouse so it's a poor design.  They should be on the back, which is completely unutilized.3) The rtx5060 isn't terribly impressive but not terrible.  It feels comparable to the 4060 in my 2023 model gaming laptop.  If you're gaming you'll want to use the msi center app and turn on performance mode.  By default it is in a hybrid mode managed by AI that worries too much about energy conservation...4) There is only one SSD slot so it doesn't support more than one drive which is bizarre heading into 2026.The laptop is listed a as not supporting gen5 nvme m.2 SSDs but that's not true.  I upgraded to a 2TB gen5 with no issues, however windows 11 24h2 wouldn't recognize any ssd with either the stock 4th gen 1tb or the 5th gen 2TB I installed so I had to get the IRST driver from the MSI website in order to install windows.  You'll also want to grab the other msi drivers if you're doing a fresh install because by default the USB drivers Windows 11 applies transfers data at roughly 5% of capacity.I like that the bright colorful rgbs are only on the keyboard so when the lid is closed you're not lighting up the whole house at night.I also upgraded the ram from 16gb ddr5 to 32gb and upgraded the wifi from the 6e card to the BE200 wifi 7 card.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent laptop but disable MS OneDrive immediately
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Excellent laptop, shipped and delivered on time.  Nearly perfect.  Make sure you get Windows 11 Pro; 11 Home sux and will attempt to stop you from loading browsers other than MS Edge, and will only load games from the MS store.  REMOVE/BLOCK/NEUTRALIZE MS OneDrive IMMEDIATELY, however.  This malware program, supposedly for backup,  will send files from your machine to "The Cloud," like it did with my website and password file, causing a security emergency that took me 2 1/2 hours to fix.  Other than MS's programming, this is the best laptop I have ever owned or seen and I highly recommend it.  Sound quality is excellent, and I have not had it lock up on me yet, even though I have the bad habit of opening a LOT of tabs.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great gaming laptop with too many bells and whistles.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great gaming performance. No issues with boot, apps, or any of the really important stuff. This laptop is physically very large, be prepared.If you are ordering one of these, my advice is to get more RAM and HDD space than you think that you need. For me, 32G Ram and 2GB HDD was more than I had and leaves enough room to do more.This laptop can run hot when gaming. Most "Chill Pads" are too small for the G18. It would be great if Asus would either design and sell one or recommend  a chill pad that works with a laptop this large.The Chill Pad I ordered fits, but I had to modify the foam so as not to block any vents.Also, I have a small fan to evacuate the hot air from behind the laptop. That made the most difference.Not 5 stars because of the keyboard. The translucent keys are obnoxious. That and  the changes versus a standard keyboard; No right CTRL key, rearranged the keys above the number pad, smaller 0 key, etc. That and the obnoxious "Aura" leds. That feature needs an Off switch.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good OLED 240hz gaming laptop, a bit pricey considering the specs.Good OLED 240hz gaming laptop, a bit pricey considering the specs.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: A bit pricey for the specs, but all things considered I'd say worth it. It's OLED and 240hz refresh rate with a powerful gpu, these three factors alone somewhat justify the price tag, the cpu and storage could be a bit better, but you can upgrade the storage later if need be mostly for faster read write speeds. It's a pretty powerful Gaming laptop, it will handle most recent games at mid to ultra settings give and take in certain games based on it's demand for cpu processing like World of Warcraft. Ideally if you are playing a game that has huge maps, and loading information this will start to struggle but only slightly, these read and write times can be improved with a little tweeking here and there. Temperatures stay at a decent range, and fans are very quiet. The battery life is quite exceptional based on how you are gaming i.e. higher graphics settings in game. This Laptop can support HDR which is pretty impressive and does so pretty effectively without draining too much of the battery or processing speeds. It's very sleek, light, and portable for on the go gaming. To sum up, the price tag is really the only debatable decision for this purchase, if you have the extra cash to spend and want a good gaming laptop, that can be upgraded, play and stream videos, and other mid functions such as light video editing, music production, and coding this could be just what you are looking for, but if you have the money and the knowledge and don't care about portability you are much better off building your own PC with the money you can make a stronger faster gaming PC to do all these features and more.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Alienware 18 Area-51 Gaming Laptop 

Alienware Area-51 gaming laptops are engineered for maximum power, packed with innovation, and encased in other-worldly design. 
18" WQXGA 2560x1600 300Hz 3ms 100% DCI-P3 500 nit, NVIDIA G-SYNC + Advanced Optimus, FHD Camera Display
Intel Core Ultra 9 processor 275HX (24-Core, 36MB Total Cache, 2.7GHz to 5.4GHz)
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 8GB GDDR7
1TB NVMe M.2 PCIe Gen4 SSD
32GB, 2x16GB, DDR5, 6400MT/s Memory
Playtime. Anytime. 

Play the latest games with graphics that rival reality. Play with players on console. Play with the peripherals that you love. When it comes to playing your way, Windows 11 makes it happen. 
The new performance precedent 

Alienware Area-51 gaming laptops are engineered for maximum power, packed with innovation, and encased in otherworldly design. By fusing an advanced thermal strategy, increasing airflow and elevating power with Intel Core Ultra HX processors and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptop GPUs, we're bringing alien-class performance to the most passionate gamers. 
Unapologetic power 

Area-51 was intentionally designed to reach new performance horizons by enabling higher graphics and processor power limits. Total Performance Power (TPP) can reach up to 190W in our Alienware 18 Area-51. With more power provided to the silicon components, gamers can run their games on the highest settings. 
Up to 115W: Total Graphics Power means higher GPU performance with more realistic gameplay. 
Up to 75W: CPU Thermal Design Power means full power devoted towards processing tasks in real-time. 
Game changing graphics 

Step into the future of gaming and creation with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptop GPUs, powered by NVIDIA Blackwell and AI. RTX 50 Series with NVIDIA Max-Q delivers optimized battery life and performance and jaw-dropping graphics—perfect for those who demand the extraordinary on the go. 
Ray Tracing Redefined: Experience cinematic realism with full ray tracing and breakthrough neural rendering technologies. 
AI-Boosted Gameplay: Unleash next-level performance and image quality with DLSS 4. 
Intelligent processing 

Intel Core Ultra HX processors integrate CPU, built-in GPU, and NPU into a single package designed for AI acceleration and balanced performance across your favorite things to do. 
CPU: Ensures everything runs smoothly and as expected; like controlling non-player characters, calculating realistic physics, translating a button press into an action, and triggering sound effects at the right time in the game. 
NPU: Uses AI with compatible livestreaming software to remove your background. 
Supercharged data stream 

Multitasking for Gamers and Creators: With two SO-DIMM slots designated for DDR5 system memory, Area-51 laptops can support up to 64GB of memory. This amount exceeds the needs of a majority of popular games but can assist gamers who create where multiple applications may need to be ran at the same time such as video editing, streaming, and playing large scale games simultaneously. 
Total Command 

Control more than ever with Alienware Command Center. 
Convenient presets: Maximize your gameplay with performance presets for the power you need. 
Performance overlay: Manage and see CPU, GPU, memory and thermals stats without exiting the game. 
AlienFX: Customize your set up with lighting settings that extend to all your Alienware accessories. 
AlienVision: Toggle external Alienware monitor hardware-based overlays on/off to help you focus on the targets at hand. 
Introducing the Cryo-Chamber 

Developed by our engineers, Area-51’s new Cryo-Chamber structure, located at the bottom of the laptop, focuses air to the core components where it matters the most. The Cryo-Chamber props up the laptop and introduces a much larger air intake, promoting increased airflow. This structure, combined with more copper, enable a higher power ceiling, up to 190W TPP, without raising acoustics. 
Performance Driven Thermals 

Marathon gaming requires absolute power. Our advanced cooling technology, Alienware Cryo-tech, is designed to maintain system stability even during the most demanding sessions. 
More copper, less heat 

With up to 48% more copper in weight than our previous 18" laptops and a vapor chamber that is 4x larger the Alienware 18 Area-51 dynamically balances heat across up to 7 heat pipes making it our most performance forward 18" laptop to date. 
Element 31 thermal interface 

Encapsulated gallium-silicone across the CPU, dissipates heat fast, allowing you to take on marathon gaming sessions with ease. 
Advanced features tailored to gamers 

Uniquely engineered to reflect the limitless possibilities within. 
Enhanced switches: Ultra Low-Profile Keyboard with AlienFX per-key lighting. 
Enhanced touchpad: Larger, multi-point and precise touchpad. 
Smarter sound: Amplified Dolby Atmos Quad speakers deliver dynamic and spatial audio. 
Advanced dynamic lighting 

Ambient AlienFX lighting inspired by the aurora borealis takes on color and movement which reflects across surfaces to create an otherworldly experience. The masterful layering of materials marks a new level of technical ability and design sophistication.

aplus content video
Zero hinge innovation 

A more robust closure and nearly invisible hinge creates a floating display. Engineered for strength and sophistication this patent pending design drives motion in the radial direction and telescopes out, enabling an adaptive rear design that features translucent materials and new AlienFX lighting. 
Bringing comfort to the forefront 

Our new Area-51 laptops combine mystery and otherworldly design with fluid contours and soft surfaces that inspires comfortable gameplay for hours. 
Contours: Fluid design contours with thoughtful edges provide enhanced tactile feeling. 
V-Rail edges: Easy and comfortable open and closing for the lid of your laptop. 
Pillowed palm rest: Seamless pillowed palm rest redefines comfort during any gaming session. 
Next-gen hardware in every aspect 

Incredible Battery: A new, larger, 96WHr Lithium Ion battery enables fast charging and uses Alienware Battery Defender technology to optimise power consumption. The Alienware 18 Area-51 can deliver up to 6 hours and 43 minutes of battery life. 
Superior Wi-Fi: Area-51 laptops come standard with Wi-Fi 7 technology ensuring high peak rates and low latency. 
Versatile Thunderbolt: New Thunderbolt 4 technology provides the best connectivity to all your external devices.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great laptop but know what you’re getting! (Great value for the price)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you're hesitating about buying this Asus ROG Strix, don't doubt it—buy it. I’ve been using it for a month now, and it has been excellent since day one. Here is a review coming from my experience:Pros:Performance: The CPU and GPU are incredibly powerful; they handle everything with almost 0 problems.Audio Quality: The Dolby Atmos implementation is excellent, even without external speakers or headphones. It sounds crisp and immersive.Build & Cooling: As expected from the premium ROG line, the chassis quality is top-class, and the cooling system keeps thermals well-managed.Screen: For the $1,299 price point, it’s a great panel. It’s vibrant and clear, though I wish it were slightly brighter.Cons:Windows Hello: It’s a nice feature, but it’s inconsistent. It frequently fails to recognize me, forcing me to use my PIN. It should be more reliable, especially in low light.Network Port (LAN): I’ve noticed the physical port feels a bit loose. Sometimes the cable loses connection, which forces a switch to Wi-Fi, incredibly annoying during gaming. I have to position the cable just right to keep it stable. (I recommend checking if your unit has this issue early on).RAM: 16GB is starting to feel limiting in 2026. For a smooth, future-proof experience, I highly recommend upgrading to 32GB or more.Recommendation:-Use it with the AC on if you want to cool your laptop enough so this one doesn't suffer of thermal throttling and if you can afford a great laptop cooler buy it (I recommend Llano coolers.)-Boot from 0 (if you know how to do it): This is for you to start in 0 and avoid Asus services and extra-softwares that it comes by default. Use G-Helper instead of Armoury Crate btw.Verdict: I have zero regrets. Despite the minor issues with the LAN port and the webcam sensor, this laptop is a beast and offers fantastic value for the money.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Run, run as FAST as you can from ASUS
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If I could give this laptop zero stars I would and hopefully this review saves someone from ever buying an ASUS laptop or any of their products. I bought this laptop in late September of 2025 as a birthday present for myself and by early-mid December I was already having issues. The cpu and gpu were both running at 100% usage, the cpu was getting up to 89 degrees Celsius, and my fps was dropping to single digits (anywhere from 1-8 fps constantly) any time I would try to play ANY game, to try to help that, I bought an $80 laptop cooling stand to try to cool the laptop down and it was STILL reaching high 80’s. I sent the computer in for repair under warranty back in December of 2025. I got the laptop back and everything was somehow worse and the repair summary they sent said that all they did was change a pad and add tape. I got tired of messing with it so I didn’t do anything with it for 3 months. It is now march of 2026 as I’m writing this review and I just sent the laptop back for repair a second time last weekend. I got an email yesterday saying that their “repair technicians” (if you can even call them that) found no issues with the unit and they will be sending it back unrepaired unless I provide more information even though I’ve been on the phone with ASUS around 7 times in the past week confirming what I sent the laptop in for. Do NOT buy anything from asus, it’ll save you money and time. Go buy yourself a better computer from a company that actually cares about and helps their customers.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: There are much better laptops out there for the money
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Avoid this product.  It's the most disappointing laptop I've ever had.Tl;dr: The laptop mostly functions as expected, but there is something seriously wrong with the networking that I believe is software related.  This was fixed for me by reinstalling Windows.  The installation it came with had some kind of networking issue that I couldn't resolve without wiping the pre-configured drive. The other major issue is the keyboard malfunctions by periodically cutting out for 30 seconds at a time every 30 minutes or so.  This is kind of weird because I didn't have this issue initially.  The keyboard issue may be related to firmware.  It may only have issues at lower power states, but I'm not sure.  All firmware and drivers are up to date though.Pros:It's powerful, has a good battery life, moderate weight, etc.Cons:Armory create is pretty terrible.  I have heard people complaining about it for years and now I see why.It came installed with McAfee spyware. Why do that?I can't figure out what the problem is yet, but SMB file transfer speeds are impossibly slow.  I can move files between PCs at 20MB/s at best (often 5-10MB/s).  Usually I can only use about 150Mbps of bandwidth.  I was hoping to get close to the 2.5Gbe speeds or the Wifi 7 speeds, but no... it's profoundly useless to move large files.  Every other PC I have on the network is blazing fast, but this laptop operates at 20 year old speeds.  Iperf3 shows fast speeds, which I admittedly find confusing, so maybe there is some kind of significant SMB configuration issue that I don't understand with the OEM windows installation/configuration.  I'm going to try to reinstall windows and figure out how to at least get 10 year old network speeds.  That'd be an improvement over how it is now.I would avoid this laptop as it's been a painful experience to have incredibly terrible networking on a laptop.  I'm thinking about trying to RMA it if reinstalling Windows won't help, but I'm afraid with Asus' RMA reputation, it's worth just selling it at a loss if there are issues.Update:I was able to get the networking to work better by wiping the primary drive and reinstalling Windows without whatever bloat it came with.  The Wi-fi is still trash, with super low speeds, but the ethernet port is working properly after wiping the Windows installation it came with.  Unfortunately the other major issue I've run into is the keyboard stops working periodically, and this happens often (roughly every 30 mins).  It'll cut off to where no key works for roughly 30 seconds then functions normally again.  There are many people complaining about that for years, so I think it's a widespread issue.  I don't have a solution to this problem yet, so I'm thinking about starting the RMA process to try that route.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 24, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast, large, hot, and $500 more expensive than in 2025.  Beware the included software.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is an extremely fast gaming laptop, and has fulfilled its duties admirably.  I did add a second SSD for more storage, but other than that it's in its original form.Pros:- Fast, responsive screen with a good size and good quality.  No ghosting and good color.  Fully supports variable refresh rates.- Fast GPU/CPU combination when using the dGPU (5080) for games.  More than fast enough for everything else when using the iGPU (built-in Intel graphics).- Easy to access the slots/sockets for adding RAM and SSDs.  This also helps if you have to maintain the laptop or repair it.  Makes it easy to clean out the dust and hair.- The ports for connectivity are good enough.  It doesn't add a ton of separate HDMI and DisplayPort connections, but there's enough to use it as a desktop replacement.  The USB ports are fast and provide enough power for every peripheral I use.Cons:- Asus Armory Crate is pretty much required for performance mode switching, RGB selection, fan modes, etc.  It's VERY intrusive, and is defaulted in the BIOS to automatically install in Windows.  You can turn that setting off, but you'll still need the software if you want to control that stuff.  It might even be a form of spyware, so be careful and do your research.- No HDR for the built-in screen.  Yes, HDR works on a monitor, but the included display doesn't support it.- It gets HOT when gaming.  At max performance mode, run the fans at max speed and keep it off your lap.- It WILL build up dirt/dust/debris in the fan.  Keep it clean or you'll have to replace the fan eventually.- If you plan on running Linux on it, the sound output through the built-in speakers can eventually become an issue, as the Linux drivers seem to get confused due to the GPU's drivers for passing sound over HDMI.  Yes, this is very technical, but if you plan on using Linux, I expect you'll be able to understand the issue.I bought this for less than it costs now, since the prices have increased due to GPU/RAM/CPU silicon is being earmarked for AI server farms.  Value at the time was absolutely great.  Now?  Everything costs too much.  You might be happier with a slightly-slower GPU like a 5070ti in a major sales event like Memorial Day.  Right now, it's probably just too expensive.  I can't really call it a good value when it's $500+ more expensive than it was a year ago.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 25, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am very happy with this laptop! It plays everything I throw at it without a hiccup. This is my second Asus G16 system, the first of which I gave to my wife since her original laptop died. Other than some really superficial details, it is hard tell them apart at first glance. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great overall, some annoyances that can mostly be fixed.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Only been using for one week, but the experience so far has been great. Here's a few things I care about:Laptop Build (5/5). Keyboard is snappy and feels good to type or game on. Track pad is very precise and allows me to read, zoom-in, and traverse webpages very easily. Laptop has some good weight to it and won't move around on a slick surface. Screen has a robust pivot and will move exactly where you want it to and stay there. USBs are as advertised, but there is a physical switch to turn camera off which is really nice. All ports are on the left and right, and the power plug is not a circular power cord, rather a rectangular one which this laptop deserves. It's a good, solid connection, not going to slip out.Heat Tolerance (5/5). So far, I have had no problem running games on ultra settings. Neither the power brick nor the laptop itself has gotten too hot, just warm. The heat is dissipated behind the screen, pointed away, which is a great location for it. Noise level for maintaining good temperature is great, better than my prior laptop.Screen/Color Quality (5/5). The screen is beautiful and definitely bright enough. There is built-in color correction that is a game changer, and compared to previous laptops it is not even close. It's great to read or play games on, and there's lots of options.Gaming Quality (4.5/5). When just playing a game alone, it does great. I have played games on Ultra quality and the FPS doesn't drop below 240 Hz, which is the max refresh rate of the screen. There are certainly more powerful systems out there, but this one is excellent for a laptop. I sometimes will have many Youtube videos open, a discord call, etc., and it still keeps this performance. However, the graphics cards struggles slightly when in the GPU optimized for gaming. Animated GIFs in discord will sometimes glitch out when using this GPU. Additionally, when closing out a game, there is a lag spike that can takes a few seconds, which is the system switching out GPUs. These are minor things, but expect some annoyances. Outside of these instances, it has been perfect.Operating System and Software (3/5). The systems comes packaged with a bunch of bloatware, and Windows 11 shoves ads down your throat at every opportunity. However, I was able to uninstall all bloatware, and through a few hours of searching the internet, I was able to suppress all of Windows 11's ads. I was also able to remove Copilot, which is a must. I immediately went to install a new browser (Edge is still terrible), but the system seemed to keep on setting my default BACK to edge. It took 4 or 5 tries for it to stick. Clearly, MS doesn't want you making this change. The same is for the default search engine, which kept on going back to the default, when I wanted DuckDuckGO. I was also able to uninstall McAfee (also terrible) and put on Malwarebytes. It comes with a subscription, but you couldn't pay me to that software. Overall this is pretty standard procedure for any new Windows machine, but it stank a little more this time.Battery Performance (2/5). When the system is on battery, don't expect to play games. For reference, Bloons TD6 is too much, and it switches between normal speed and chugging along like a device from 5 generations ago. It clearly is not able to take it, nor optimized for it. You can do other things like watch videos or whatever for maybe a few hours. I highly recommend keeping this thing plugged in 100% of the time.Given that all the bloatware and Windows 11 annoyances were able to be fixed, and that battery performance isn't much of a factor for me, I still give this laptop a 5/5. It's a fantastic choice overall. It really feels like a medium performance desktop crammed into a laptop.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on September 28, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: An Absolute Masterpiece of Portable Power
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After an exhaustive search for a true desktop replacement that refused to compromise, my journey has emphatically ended with the Lenovo Legion Pro 7i. To call this just a "gaming laptop" feels like a disservice; it's a meticulously engineered marvel that redefines what's possible in a portable form factor.The performance is, in a word, staggering. The combination of the Intel Core Ultra 9 and the RTX 5070 Ti GPU chews through every modern title I've thrown at it without breaking a sweat. Even notoriously demanding games run with a fluidity that has to be seen to be believed, maintaining high frame rates that take full advantage of the display.And let's talk about that display, because it deserves its own chapter. The 16-inch 2.5K OLED panel is breathtaking. The infinite contrast with true, deep blacks and the sheer vibrancy of the colors make every visual experience, from gaming to content creation, utterly captivating. Paired with a silky-smooth 240Hz refresh rate, the clarity and responsiveness are simply on another level. It has genuinely ruined other screens for me.What's equally impressive is the thermal management. Even when pushing it hard using Lenovo Vantage's preset performance modes, the laptop never feels like it's overheating. It gets warm, as expected from a high-performance machine, but the heat is managed so well that the keyboard and typing area remain remarkably comfortable. I've personally tweaked the custom power profiles, and the level of customization has allowed me to optimize performance to even greater lengths, all without the hardware risks of traditional overclocking.What truly seals the deal is the incredible value proposition. In a market saturated with overpriced options, this machine feels like a hidden gem. It trades blows with laptops costing hundreds more, offering flagship-tier performance and features without the exorbitant price tag. Lenovo has found the perfect sweet spot.Every aspect of the Legion Pro 7i feels premium, from its solid aluminum chassis to the scorching-fast storage. If I had to pinpoint the one area where a budget-conscious decision was made, it's the plastic trackpad. Frankly, it's a brilliant choice. In a machine this powerful, it's the only noticeable compromise, and for any serious user who brings their own mouse, it's a complete non-issue. It shows Lenovo put the money where it truly counts. They haven't just built a great laptop; they've earned a new loyal customer. If you are on the fence, consider this your sign. This is the one. An unreserved five-star recommendation.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A portable and solid Linux laptop.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was in the market for a small laptop to fulfill my "Linux tablet dreams".  I knew ahead of time that this laptop would be under powered compared to other laptops that I own but the purpose of this was to maximize portability.  Furthermore, I'm using this for general web browsing, reading my RSS feeds, and the occasional YouTube or Netflix.  This fits the bill.  The keyboard is the perfect size and I don't feel that it's cramped in any way.I went with my preferred Linux flavor of Fedora.  I initially opted for Fedora Xfce Spin due to how lightweight it is, but my Xfce skills are terrible and I struggled to get the screen working properly.  So I moved onto Fedora KDE Plasma.  KDE Plasma worked out of the box for the most part.  There is still some tweaking that needs to be done but screen orientation can be adjusted, accelerometer works out of the box, touch screen works, etc.I'll point out a few sticking points that have yet to be resolved, which I'll still include in the pros/cons below.One is that the battery life isn't great, this wasn't news to me.  I think about 3-4 hours of web browsing and I'll throw it back on the charger when it's at about 35%-40%.  It could go much longer than that but I'm opting to plug in around that percentage.  You cannot set charge limits (I'd like to max out at 80% and stop), but as I understand it this is something that the BIOS needs to support.  I'm unsure how to resolve this.The screen is natively in portrait mode (1200x1920 10:16 instead of 1920x1200 16:10).  This means Grub will be in portrait mode until the kernel loads.  After installing your distro be sure to go into your display configuration and set the screen orientation to auto and uncheck "only in tablet mode".  Then the screen will rotate freely despite the resolution expressed the way it is.  The screen maxes out at 50Hz but some have gotten it to go up to 95Hz on other distros like Arch.  Seems to remain at 50Hz in Fedora.When you fold the screen all the way back into "tablet mode" the keyboard and touchpad remain enabled.  While you can manually disable the touchpad, there should be a way to disable it when folding the screen.  I don't know if this is a hardware, OS, or software implementation issue.What I bought this for:- Lightweight Linux "tablet".- Ultra portability for travel- General web browsing, RSS, occasional YouTube and Netflix.Pros:- Linux compatible.  Fedora KDE Plasma works great out of the box.- Lightweight- Keyboard is excellent- Metal construction feels great in the hand.- Price was reasonableCons:- Battery does not last long.- Can't set battery charge limits (I'm assuming this is a hardware limitation and not an OS limitation).- Screen is natively in portrait mode (not a deal breaker and only a minor annoyance during boot)- Keyboard and touchpad remain enabled when folding the screen all the way back into "tablet mode".
