N29（Atom Z3735F）とYoga Book(Atom x5-Z8550)なのですが、前者は言うまでも無く発売当時から動作は快適から程遠かったもののキーボードとモニタが取り外せて尚且つカッチリとその二つが安定して固定されるので発売から7年以上たった今でも（動作の激重さを除けば）不具合無く使えています。流石は世界に誇るmade inJapan！！…（と思って念のため本体裏を見たらmade in Chinaでした笑）そして店頭でその驚きの厚み（薄さ）やスタイリッシュさで一目惚れして購入したのが後者（Yoga book）で、こちらもCPUはAtomなので今では決して快適な動作とは言い難いものの、逆に折りたたんでタブレット型にしても今時のタブレットと遜色のない厚みでデザインも今でもお気に入りなのですが1年ほど前からバッテリーが膨張しだしてしまい交換も容易では無い事から現在使用を控えています。なので現状、もし出先でWindowsPCが必要になる場面だと重量は軽めで仕事用カバンに余裕で収まるレベルに小型だけど動作激重のDynabook N29か動作は超快適だけど別バッグに詰めて運ぶ必要があり本体激重のASUSのゲーミングノートと言う超極端な選択肢しかなくなってしまったのでスペックそこそこで持ち運び快適で尚且つ車中でも使いやすい（これ大事）を探していてこちらが目に留まり、色々な他機種と数日悩んだ末に購入しました。個人的にはスペック自体はもうワンランク下でも構わなかったのですが、やはりサイズ感が持ち運ぶには丁度良い事や、安めの2in1に比較的多い仕様のキーボードとモニタが物理的に固定されておらずあくまでテーブル等での使用が前提となっているタイプはそもそもモニタの角度も変えられず車中での使用ですと膝の上では不安定で使いづらいので避けました。あと、Celeron J4125は以前タイムセールで見かけてほぼ衝動買いで買ってしまったミニPCに乗っていたものと同じでメモリも全く同じの6GBだった為、現状は買ったは良いが使い道が無くて押し入れの肥やしとなっているものの、購入時に触った感触としてはセレロンとは言え動作感は悪く無いといった印象でしたので、むしろゲーム等をしないのであればモバイルノートとしては十分すぎる位の高性能だと感じました。見た目も中々良くてサイズが小さいから余計にそう感じるのだと思いますがかなりズッシリしています。指紋認証の感度も爆速とは言いませんが悪くありません。キー配列に関しては多数の方が仰られていますがやはり慣れが必要ですね。私の場合は特にAとSを良く押し間違えてしまいます…（Aを押したつもりがSを入力）あとは＠を押したつもりがdelete等々＠はかなり変則的な位置でF6の上というかなり謎使用（苦笑Aは特に良く使う文字なので慣れるまではちょっとイライラしちゃいそうです。しかしこれは配列を極力一般的な物にする為にキーを小さくしてしまうとそれはそれで打ちにくくなってしまうので慣れてさえしまえばこちらの方が良いかも知れませんね。あとこれは名称は良くわからないのですがマウスカーソルを動かすためのボッチみたいなもの。これも使いやすいと感じるかどうかは人それぞれって感じですが、個人的には可もなく不可も無く、無いよりはあった方が良いかなって感じでした。タッチパネルなので触れるサイズならばタッチで、タッチしたい範囲が狭くて微調整したい時やダブルタップが上手くいかない時などは矢印をボッチで調整してキーの左クリックを二回押し等々で使い分けてます。大きく動かすのは面倒ですが、反応自体はかなり良いので小回りはきくってイメージでしょうか？この辺はマウスの設定で変更可能なので好みで調整すると良いと思いますが、あまり過敏にすると使いにくいと思います。画質もかなり良いと思います。ただ画面自体は小さいのでFHDの等倍表示だと老眼が入ってきた私にはかなり厳しい事と高解像度による負荷をちょっとでも減らしてその分快適性を上げようと思い倍率では無く解像度自体を少し落として使用しています。視野角もかなり広いので誰か隣に人を呼んで上や横から一緒に見て貰っても（画面が小さい故の見にくさを除けば）良く視認できます。バッテリーの持ちに関してはメインで使用している訳では無く、1日に良く使ってもトータル1～2時間なので50%を切る様な場面も無く不満に感じる事はありませんでしたが、充電自体が充電口はtype-Cではあるものの、12V2Aでの充電が必要なので一般的なスマホ用の充電器では充電出来ず、また付属の充電器は完全に専用品なので間違ってもスマホなどの充電に使わない様にしないと大変危険です。なので当然ながら一般的なモバイルバッテリーでは充電出来ず、特にC to Cケーブルでつないでいる場合は一見充電出来ているように見えても実は「PCからモバイルバッテリー側に給電」している状態になっている場合もあります。一応計算上は24W以上と1口から出力できるモバイルバッテリー+それに対応可能な充電ケーブルであれば充電は可能かとは思いますが、一般的な高速充電（PD等）可能なモバイルバッテリーでは18w～20wであり、それ以上の物もあるにはありますが値段が一気に高騰してくるので折角コストパフォーマンスの良いこの機種を買ったのにそこで更にコストを掛けてしまうのは本末転倒な気もします。なので性能的に致し方が無い事だったのかも知れませんが、出来れば充電時間は多く必要になってしまうとは思いますが一般的なスマホ用（5V-2A等、またはそこそこ対応の多い12V1.5A）に対応出来ていればモバイル用途として完璧だったでしょうね。先にも書きましたが現状ではこのバッテリー容量に関しては問題は感じていませんが、使い続けていく絵で将来的に不便を感じる場面は起こりえてしまうのでその点を差し引き☆4とさせて頂きました。

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: 初期不良に当たりましたが返品後再購入初期不良に当たりましたが返品後再購入
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: 画面はグレーで線がいっぱい。どうみても初期不良品です。ディスプレイを動かすと極稀に映りますがすぐ消えます。楽しみにしていたのにがっかり。返品して再購入後に再レビューします。追記再購入したので使い勝手をレビュー。気軽に持ち運べるWindowsが欲しくて購入。やはり小さいので、持ち運びのしやすさは最強レベル。キーボードも付いているのでタブレットのように別途キーボードを用意したりスタンドを立てたりしなくていいのはほんとストレスなくていい。この手の製品は性能が低くて使い物にならないのが一般的でしたが、Celeron N4125はギリギリ実用レベルのライン。日常使いなら使えます。RAMも6GBなので、3D CADとか動画編集は厳しいです（動きますけどね）。キーボードはかなり変態配列なので入力に苦労します。Q列とA列のキーのズレが少ないので、感覚的にズレてしまいます。また、TABキーが変な位置にあるので文字変換時にTABキーを使う人には不便（Change keyというソフトでQとTABを入れ替えると良い）。また、「ろ」のキーにアンダースコアが割当られていないので、打てません。プログラミングなどで使う人は注意。Shift+ろ  で打てるよ！と解説しているサイトがありますが、打てません。バッテリーは5時間くらい持ちます。そうそう純正の充電器はType-C形状なのに12V固定出力なので他の機器に使うとぶっ壊れると思います。12VのPD充電器が使えるので、私はダイソーの700円のアダプターを使ってます。「みろ」の名でYou Tubeにレビュー投稿しているので、よろしければご覧ください（宣伝）。

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: キーボードは標準ピッチ並みですがかなり変則
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: 「日本語キーボード」「Win11モデル」の購入です。購入前から分かっていましたし、UMPCファンとして富士通LifeUやVAIO等のUMPCも使い続けてきたので、本当にわかってはいたのですが、キーボードが打ち辛いです。これなら、GPD PocketやLet’s Note RZシリーズのように狭ピッチでいいからもうちょっと一般的な配列のキーボードにして欲しかったと思います。けれど、Intel Atomを積んだGPD Pocketに比べてJ4125はかなり快適で、出先でのリモート用途という自分の使い道には打って付けと感じています。キーボード右下(本来ならShiftキーが来る場所か)にある「ろ」キーが、PrintScreenキーに割り当てられているのはまぁ構わないのですが、肝心の「_」₍アンダースコア₎が入力できません。他の方々が言われている通りです。そこでPowerToysを入れてキーマップを変更し、「ろ」キーを押すと「＿」、Fn＋「ろ」キーを押すと「\」というようにしてみました。PrintScreenキーもつい手に、Fnキー上部、「＠」マークの右隣にある「再生・ポーズ」ボタンに移動しました。これで一応、自分に必要なキーはすべて割り当てられました。PowerToysでの割り当て時に若干苦労したので、やり方を書いておきます。PowerToysをインストール後、Keybord managerからキーマップを割り当てる際、割り当て元のキーは問題ないとして、割当先のキーに「‗」₍アンダースコア₎がありません。そこでスクリーンキーボードを出し、そちらから割当先として「_」を入力します。すると、「ろ」に「_」が割り当たります。Fn＋「ろ」がなぜ「￥」になるのかは不明ですが、入力できているので良しとします。なおプリインストールされているWin11のライセンス認証が行えません。これから販売元に問い合わせてみます。

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: そこそこ早くてコンパクト　旅用サブPCにピッタリ
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: 4コアのCPUJ4126と6GBメモリーでそこそこ早い。コンパクトで、持ち歩きに便利。30WくらいのコンパクトなUSBーcのACアダプタで使えるので、旅のお供にはおすすめ。旅先で撮影した動画をYouTubeにアップしたり、電車待ってる間動画を見たりちょっとしたゲームもできちゃいます。ポインターは操作に難があるので、ちっちゃい有線マウスを使うといいかもです。

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: SSDの拡張で行き詰まるSSDの拡張で行き詰まる
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: SSDを取り付けようにもネジの駆動部のところが私の持っている精密度ライバーセットでは開けることができない形状のようでした。星形でもないですし、これ以外の特殊なドライバーを探してみるつもりですが、どんな形状が合うんでしょうね。別途購入した512GB積みたいので、いざとなったら瞬間接着剤でドライバーとネジを固定して開けてみたいと思います。さて、今回CHUWI製のPCは２台目でして、１台目はWindowsとAndroidのデュアルブートの８インチタブレットでした。Windowsアップデートのための空き容量が作ないのと、メモリ４GBでは厳しくなってきたので、今回の購入になりました。Yogaスタイル、タブレットにもなること、type-AのUSBポートが2つ、MicroSDカードスロットが有るのがいいですね。持っているモバイルバッテリーもtype-Cで12V 2Aに対応していたので外出先などでも大丈夫そうです。キートップは欲を言えばカーソルキー並みの大きさならファンクションキーを押さずに入力できる配列にできたのでは？と思いました。記号を多用するときは入力し辛いかもしれません。◆2022/12/21追記◆プラスドライバーでSSDの取り付けが出来ました。どうやらネジの駆動部が（新品なら工場で）なめた状態だったようです。◆◆セットアップ実行しました！。Windowsのライセンスが他で使われてるとか出まして、「最近ハード変えたか」とあったのでクリックしたら、件のタブレットのアカウント使ってたので、そのWindows10のライセンスで認証されちゃいました。あれー(￣▽￣;) MiniBookのライセンスどこ行った？というわけでアカウントの使いまわしは注意です。

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Have power, will travel (anywhere I can plug this in)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: THE SHORT VERSIONThis thing is an absolute beast. It's crushed everything I've thrown at it, to the point where I'm not getting much gaming done because I just keep thinking of other things to try that I was having problems with on my old desktop.You aren't going to get better value for money for a computer for gaming right now. Desktops are so insanely overpriced that a laptop is your only option if you're familiar with the word "budget," and you aren't going to find a better price-to-performance ratio in a laptop. Buying this thing when I did really feels like catching the last chopper out of 'Nam, given the state of the industry right now.PERFORMANCE & GAMINGI got this to replace my aging desktop (3950X / RTX 3080). This laptop runs laps around it. It's so good it actually makes me mad how much it outperforms a full ATX system I spent 5 grand building 6 years ago.The Screen: I’d originally intended to hook this up to my TV when playing with a controller, but the quality of this screen made me abandon that altogether. 16:10 with 240Hz in G-Sync looks fantastic, and the color gamut on this display is not a joke. The first time I was flipping through the display modes and landed on DCI-P3, my eyes went wide and I haven't touched that again since.Forza Horizon 6: Absolutely no problems playing at higher settings than I was used to, looking significantly better than it does on my Xbox Series X. Seriously, I was shocked how good everything looked the first time I launched it on this because it was so much better than the XSX or my outgoing desktop. It's going to take a little bit for that to stop being distracting so I can focus on racing, lmaoCyberpunk 2077: I could never get this running at all on my old desktop, but it runs flawlessly at high to max settings on this with dozens of mods loaded. I've lost count of how many times I've played through this game on my XSX, and am really looking forward to dozens more now that I can mess around with mods!(Note: I disable ray tracing, motion blur, bloom, chromatic aberration, and lower shadow/reflection qualities immediately in every game that has said options, just as personal preference, not that any of those but the RT would have a meaningful performance impact on this. I also just flatly don't believe in framegen like DLSS, so I don't use it).(I also play Fallout 76 and Pragmata, but neither of those is as much of a challenge to run as the above, so it doesn't bear wasting your time going into detail on them. Suffice it to say, 👍👍)CONS, GRIPES, & THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW LEST YOU THINK I'M A SHILLARMOURY CRATE: A PLAGUE ON ASUS'S HOUSEThe very first thing I recommend doing upon getting past the initial setup and logging into a Windows is nuking Armoury Crate from orbit and going to GitHub to download G-Helper. I could not, for the life of me, get Armoury Crate to stop changing the color of my keyboard lights, or stop animating it at random, until I got rid of Armoury Crate and set the lighting settings through G-Helper. You'll get important driver updates through the MyAsus app anyway (and G-Helper can point out drivers that are out of date and give you direct links to downloading updates, regardless), so for the sake of your sanity, don't waste any time trying to bargain with the bloat, just get rid of it and get G-Helper.HEAT: THIS THING PRODUCES ITBlock the intakes or exhausts on this thing at your own peril. It has the most impressive bottom case design I've ever seen on a laptop, with feet raising it significantly and air channels cut every which way to draw in air from as many angles as possible, but the CPU sits between 95°C and 98°C while running Cyberpunk. You can absolutely feel it blasting out the exhaust vents, which are located near the back on either side, as if they wanted to make sure that if you're using an external mouse, they keep your mouse hand warm, whether you're a righty or a lefty! Credit to the thermal design, though, I've never once felt the keyboard get noticeably warm. I've been using a laptop stand/tray thing while gaming with this in bed or on the couch, and for your safety and the machine's, I highly recommend you do the same. I’m waiting on an IETS cooling pad to arrive before I try using it at my desk with my Odyssey so it doesn't melt into slag and damage my desk, or (more likely) throttle itself like crazy to prevent that from happening. (The community likes IETS and llano about equally from what I've seen, it just so happened there was a better deal available on the IETS when I went looking to buy one.)NOISE: REAL COMPUTERS MAKE ITThis doesn't bother me at all, but if I've learned anything from working 15 years in IT, it's that the average end user expects computers to be silent at all times, likely because they've never been anywhere near a datacenter. When you fire up a AAA game on this thing, it's going to get loud, because it has 3 small fans trying to dissipate the heat from an immense amount of TDP, and the smaller a fan is, the faster it has to spin to move more air, and the louder and higher pitch that's going to be. This is basic physics. Laws of the universe. Again, I have no problem at all with this, I expected this, I own both over-ear headphones and earbuds with active noise cancellation...I'm all set, but it bears mentioning that this monster is gunna make it known when it's working hard to make those frames for ya.BATTERYI mean, look at the specs. You're not going to want to stray far from an outlet, and you certainly don't want to ever leave home without the massive 280W charging brick. While one of its USB-C ports does allow for 100W PD, you aren't going to be gaming on that for long. I tested it, and the battery gains on a 100W charger hilariously quickly if you're running a "serious" game with settings cranked up. I got about an hour into Cyberpunk before it dropped into power saving mode, begging for a real charge.(Yes, you can set it to Eco mode and completely disable the 5070Ti to squeeze a few extra minutes out of a charge, but that's not what you're buying this for. I forgot I was testing Eco mode once and launched Cyberpunk, then laughed for the full 5 minutes it took to force quit it so I could turn the GPU back on, which took a couple clicks and then the game loaded in seconds.)KEYBOARD & THE TRACKPAD NUMPAD GIMMICKI don't like that it doesn't have a real numpad, it seems ridiculous that they couldn't fit one in given the size of this thing, and the mode-switching trackpad is a gimmick. Nobody who wants to use a numpad is ever going to say "oh, that works just as well." If you're right-handed and lazily scrolling through websites, prepare yourself to occasionally trigger it by accident.Amusing sidenote: If you connect an external keyboard and hit numlock, it lights up the numpad mode on the trackpad, making it the dramatic, overwhelming winner for "biggest numlock light I've ever seen." Speaking of indicator lights...THE BLINKING INDICATOR LIGHTSThe little status indicator lights that computers often have are not so little on this, are directly under the display, facing directly at you, are bright, and at least one is blinking at all times. Asus removed the functionality that allowed you to turn them off in software that existed on prior models, and no, even G-Helper can't save you here. The community response has been "cut some tape to fit over them." For now, I've covered all but a little dot on each one, but I might cover the disk indicator light entirely because really....it just blinks constantly, and the information conveyed by that wildly outweighs the annoyance, in practice, in my opinion. (Your mileage may vary based on how susceptible to annoyance you are and how well you can tune things out.)HDMI PORT VS. USB-CThe HDMI port wasn't as useful as I'd hoped. I tried hooking it up to my Odyssey 32:9 at my desk, and while it would push a full 5120x1440, it couldn't do HDR or G-Sync, and it was locked at 60Hz. For productivity, this is absolutely fine. Great, even. For gaming? I wasn't thrilled.The Fix: Get a USB-C to DisplayPort cable. The USB-C ports on this thing are wired DIRECTLY to the GPU. The instant I plugged that cable in, I was back to full functionality for my wildly unreasonable monitor, with 49-120Hz VRR, HDR, and full G-Sync compatibility showing in the Nvidia app.IN CONCLUSIONThe day I pulled the trigger on buying this was immediately after its replacement was announced, with no AMD CPU option and costing nearly twice as much because it's targeted exclusively at generating slop, not gaming. I spent weeks looking, and couldn't find a better price-to-performance ratio. For all the aforementioned faults, I love it. It's not perfect, but neither is the world we're living in. Happy gaming, folks.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE 2/4/26:  DO NOT BUY THIS. DO NOT BUY FROM THIS SELLER. The device was 3 weeks old when it stopped working. This seller will not honor the warranty they supposedly offer in place of the HP warranty, the HP warranty they invalidate because this seller opened the device and upgraded hardware, (find that listed somewhere). The seller refunded ~$150less on a device that broke after 3 weeks because I didn’t have the original packaging, because I didn’t plan for the device to break after 3 weeks of use. I literally asked for a replacement; they refused. Told me since I opened a return, that’s all they could do. They told me I could get the refund and buy it again; they raised the price by $150, so my net loss, their additional profit would then be $300…on an $800 laptop.  They won’t tell you before you send it back how much the penalty is for not having the box; that’s fully in their hands, they got to decide how much a cardboard box is worth…apparently ~$150. Pretty good profit to get your product back to fix and resell again. ESSENTIALLY, I WAS LEGALLY ROBBED OF ~$150 BY THIS SELLER. DISGUSTED AMAZON HAS VENDORS LIKE THIS. BTW; I saved the chat thread.Update 1/26:  got device back from HP with a letter. apparently HP won’t honor the warranty because the seller invalidates that warranty when they open the device and memory and hard drive to it. The seller won’t bother to tell you that, even when you open a return with them and tell them it’s broken, tell them you’re sending to HP. Never stopped me. Wasted 3 weeks sending to HP when it had no HP warranty.Update 1/20:  HP won’t honor warranty. Says there’s damage “customer induced.”  Didn’t include photos or evidence. I have asked for the photos, evidence, “what broke”. Quoted me $400+ to fix…my brand new, “under warranty” laptop.  There was no physical damage to the device. It just stopped working.NEVER BUYING ANYTHING HP AGAIN.DUDE, I’M GETTING A DELL!OriginalRight now...not happy.  Worked fine...for a few weeks.  Recieved on 11/18, been dead since Monday 12/8.  No event, nothing  of note, it just wouldn't power on for Monday fun.  It decided to not power on and only flash the CAPS LOCK button.No removable battery.  No specific support references for THIS model.  Good luck finding that as anything other than a "possible hardware issue".  Good luck getting support from HP on their website; it's like they hide the button to open a ticket, while telling you there is still ~6 months of warranty on your device.I've worked in IT for over 35 years. I have opened and fixed hundreds of laptops; this one I am afraid of damaging and not getting a refund if that's the path.  It doesn't have to be this hard.  I can't lay this is on the seller; unfortunately, this seems to be an HP "budgetary device" thing.  HP, don’t sell devices that won't sustain after the first month, then hide the warranty information so the user can't declare a warranty fix. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Alright, so I just got my hands on the MSI Crosshair A16, and it's exactly what I expected from MSI – a no-nonsense, solid machine. This is the 16-inch model with the Ryzen 9 8940HX, an RTX 5070, 32GB RAM, and a 1TB NVMe SSD. First impressions out of the box are that it feels well-built, sturdy, and ready to get to workWhat really stands out is the performance. The RTX 5070 handles pretty much everything I throw at it with ease, and that 2.5K QHD+ 240Hz display is a treat for the eyes. Games look smooth and sharp, and even just everyday browsing feels snappier. MSI might not always have the flashiest designs, but they consistently deliver on internal components and build quality, which is what matters most to me.For anyone looking for a powerful gaming laptop that prioritizes function over form, this Crosshair is a fantastic option. It's not about the RGB light show or the thinnest chassis; it's about getting consistent, reliable performance. This laptop delivers value where it counts.If you're already familiar with MSI's reputation for building durable, high-performing machines, this Crosshair continues that . It’s a great pick for someone who wants to invest in a powerful laptop without paying extra for unnecessary bells and whistles. Just pure, unadulterated performance.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Insane performance, but definitely feels like a plastic budget buildInsane performance, but definitely feels like a plastic budget build
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this laptop purely for the specs, and on that front, it absolutely delivers.The Good:The combination of the Ryzen 9 and the RTX 5070 is a total beast. Finally having 12GB of VRAM on a 70-series card makes a massive difference for high-end gaming. The 240Hz QHD+ screen is gorgeous, incredibly smooth, and bright enough to use anywhere. Plus, if you like upgrading your own gear, it’s super easy to pop the bottom panel off to add more RAM or a second SSD.The Bad:You can instantly tell where MSI saved money. The chassis is entirely plastic and is an absolute magnet for fingerprints and hand oils—you'll be wiping it down constantly. When you’re gaming, the fans sound like a jet engine, totally drowning out the pretty weak built-in speakers, so a headset is mandatory.Also, the included 240W power brick runs incredibly hot. During heavy gaming sessions, the laptop actually pulls so much power that the battery will very slowly drain even while plugged in.Verdict:If you plan to leave this plugged in at a desk with a headset on, the raw performance per dollar is hard to beat. But if you want a premium, quiet, premium-feeling machine to carry around daily, you might want to look elsewhere.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very good, in this market.Very good, in this market.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This MSI Crosshair A16 HX laptop is one of the latest in the mid-range Crosshair line, and the TLDR is that it's pretty good. I say pretty good, because it's hard to rationalize where it stands in terms of value because the prices keep going up on these laptops due to the RAM/SSD crisis. I had just gotten a gaming laptop 6 months ago, and this is more expensive, and inferior in terms of spec. Now, I recognize none of us has a time machine to go back and grab something more affordable last year, but the price still stings here.But let's break it down. The laptop comes pretty well packaged, with another box around it for extra protection. Inside there’s not much. Just a laptop in a plastic baggie, and a 240W power brick and detachable power cable. Just taking the laptop out of the box resulted in some nice, oily fingerprints (despite clean hands), so expect to be wiping this down a lot. The chassis is all plastic as far as I can tell, so there’s none of the premium feel that you get with a e.g. Lenovo Legion Pro 7 that I also have.Port selection is good, but not remarkable. On the left side you have the AC adapter port, 2x USB-C 3.2 Gen.2 (you can charge up to 100W with these - tested), - with DisplayPort capability, too. On the right side you have 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen. 1. On the rear, RJ-45 (only 1 Gbit), HDMI 2.1, and another USB-A 3.2 Gen. 2 port.Unfortunately there’s no Thunderbolt here, and no 2.5 Gbit ethernet. The laptop weighs just a hair under 5lbs, and feels pretty well balanced when holding it. There is absolutely no RGB on the exterior of the case at all, and whether you like the graphic on the front is going to be very subjective. It’s definitely quite gamer-y, which isn’t usually my scene in terms of case aesthetic. I prefer a more muted shell. Also a peculiar choice to have one corner rubber pad in bright blue, but that’s what we get. From the rear it looks like someone squashed a dog toy under the laptop. Hey, I didn’t ask for that!Inside we have more gamer-y graphics (still not a fan) and also we have a decent enough keyboard (not tons of key travel, but not bad). These keys are very quiet, so if you like to game in bed, your partner won’t likely complain about this, which is nice if you’re a night-time gamer. The WASD keys are also quite gamer-y and translucent. The RGB setup for the keyboard is a tad lacking, with no per-key RGB which you get on other laptops in this price range, which is disappointing. Just zonal adjustments here. The trackpad is quite large, and very responsive. I’m used to terrible trackpads on Windows laptops so this was pleasantly surprising. Oh, and for those wondering, the "AMD" sticker peeled off without leaving residue, the "GeForce" sticker took a little rubbing to get the goop up, and the "HDMI" sticker was easily removed. In any case, a fingernail and a finger rub is all you need for a clean sticker-less look.System setup was very easy. The laptop will not initially power on until the power cable is connected (despite having some charge), but as soon as it is plugged in, all systems are a go. Windows setup is fairly rudimentary, and doesn’t take long, and there are a few updates along the way that you can cancel and do later if you prefer.Once setup, there is just a few pieces of bloatware software (Norton, looking at you), but these only took a moment to uninstall. At this point, you’ll be able to control the screen brightness, volume, and keyboard brightness (4 levels, - or off). That’s when you’ll notice the light on the power button, that’s a bit annoying, and not brightness adjustable. It will alternate between white and orange, depending on whether the system is using the integrated Intel GPU or the Nvidia RTX 5070 discrete GPU. This is annoying because depending on what you’re doing it will switch between the two often, and it’s very, very distracting to see this orange light flash to white, and then back to orange all the time. You can lock the system to one GPU or the other rather than this hybrid system (which is ideal), but you have to reboot to switch to one or other GPU exclusively. I hope we see a firmware update to disable the light entirely, or dim it at minimum.The screen is really, really good. It’s a 16:10 1600p IPS display at 240hz, with very minimal clouding, - one of the best I've used in that regard. Unfortunately, there’s no GSync of any sort, which is surprising at this price point, but there we are. That said, it gets very, very bright, and motion handling is excellent. Gamers should be happy here, especially if poor LCD motion handling is something they are sensitive to (I’m talking about you, Nintendo Switch 2). Above the screen there is a webcam that works well enough, and has a physical switch to turn off the camera, which I like to see on laptops. Oh, and you can open the screen with one hand. The one downside is it doesn't get super dim, but that shouldn't be an issue for most.Speakers run along the top, behind the keyboard, and they are, for lack of a better word - awful. Very tinny/thin. Sure, they’ll do in a pinch (speakers usually do), but they are bad. Use headphones. You’ll want to use headphones anyway given this isn’t the quietest of laptops. It’s absolutely in line with other gaming laptops, which means twin fans running most of the time from around 2000rpm to 5500rpm-ish at the highest level. I will give MSI credit, though: these fans are a low pitch, and low pitch is good for least amount of annoyance, as it’s much more easy to tune out. At the 1975rpm default speed, they're not disturbing at all.The charger is only 240W, which comes as a major surprise given the power output of the CPU and GPU. Do not expect much, if any charging when gaming at all, and the charger gets SUPER hot when doing so. I was having a play session in “Trails in the Sky, Chapter 1”, and boy did that charger get crazy hot. On the plus side, it’s a much smaller brick than the 400W monster with my Legion Pro 7.Performance in games is very good, as you’d expect for a 5070 mobile part. There’s a question mark surrounding this 8GB variant of GPU, but for most games, especially at 1600p, I don’t expect it to much be much of an issue, and it wasn’t in my testing. Still, it’s a tad niggling to know that there’s a 12GB variant on the market in other laptops as of now.The 1TB SSD is a Micron 2500 PCIe 4 2280 drive. It’s a middle of the range drive, as you’d expect, with decent read/write speeds (around 7000MB/s read, 6000MB/s write).The Wi-Fi 6E chip I received is the RZ616, also known as the MediaTek MT7922. Absolutely zero issues with it connected to my Asus BQ16 Pro Wi-Fi 7 mesh system. On my 2 Gbit fiber internet connection (2 down, 1 up) It gets speeds in line with my Wi-Fi 7 iPhone and 6E iPad Pro, around 1.6 Gbit download, and the full 940 Mbit upload. No stability issues of any sort, even when slamming Steam with downloads.Battery life is decent for a gaming laptop. At low brightness, and on the Intel GPU specifically (to prevent hybrid mode switching), I’m averaging a little over 5 hours with light browsing. There’s also plenty enough power for work or light gaming without bringing the MSI power brick, just by using a 100W USB-C charger, and connecting via one of the ports on the left. I like being able to do that, as it means I can leave the charger in its usual place for more intensive gaming, but bring the laptop to my office and quickly connect via USB-C for work. Hibernating Windows 11 also means boot times are insanely fast, at just a few seconds.Overall, this laptop is good. There’s no question about that, and it has been rock solid over the days I've used it. But given the price, I’d have liked to see just a little more premium to the whole system. I can’t even say to wait and the prices will come down, because… that’s not true lately. So that said, as a laptop for gamers in this particular market, it’s a recommendation.4 out of 5.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a laptop that could handle a little bit of everything—work, casual streaming, and light gaming—and the ASUS Vivobook Go turned out to be the perfect choice. It’s fast, versatile, and strikes the perfect balance between something like a Chromebook and a high-end gaming laptop. I picked it up during a Cyber Monday deal, and I couldn’t be happier with the value it delivers for the price.Performance has been excellent so far. The AMD Ryzen 5 7520U processor and 8GB of RAM make this laptop responsive and reliable for everyday use. I’ve run multiple tabs, streamed videos, and even played some lighter games like Rocksmith 2014, and it’s handled everything without lagging or slowing down. It’s not a gaming powerhouse, but for what I need, it’s solid—responsive, consistent, and dependable.One thing I really appreciate is the privacy webcam cover. It’s practical and gives me peace of mind during video calls or meetings.The 15.6” screen is crisp and clear, making it a pleasure to use for both work and entertainment. Videos and documents look sharp, and the size is perfect for multitasking or just enjoying a good session. The integrated AMD Radeon Graphics also do a great job of keeping visuals smooth and consistent.Storage is another standout. The 512GB SSD gives me plenty of space for files, programs, and even a few games, and boot-up times are quick. Windows 11 Home feels intuitive and runs smoothly right out of the box, so setup was fast and hassle-free.The audio quality is pretty solid too. The ASUS SonicMaster speakers deliver clear, balanced sound, making it great for everyday tasks, music, and videos.As someone who’s spent a lot of time with tech, I can say this laptop is a winner. It’s well-built, reliable, and versatile enough to handle a bit of everything. If you’re looking for something that can balance business tasks, light gaming, and casual media consumption without breaking the bank, the Vivobook Go delivers exactly that.Overall, I’m really happy with this purchase. It does what I need it to do, looks great, and performs smoothly. ASUS nailed it here—this is a solid all-around laptop, and I’d absolutely recommend it to anyone looking for value, performance, and practical features in one package!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Didn't connect to the internet due to hardware problem
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the first laptop/notebook that hasn't started up straight out of the box. I could power it up, but I could not connect to the internet. The computer wanted me to download a driver to access internet connections. I used my old notebook with the cracked screen to search the internet for solutions to this problem. We downloaded a driver ASUS said was the one for this machine, put it on a stick and downloaded it onto the machine, followed all the directions, and nothing. x4. I spent an hour online with ASUS tech support AI chat, they said it sounds like a hardware problem, said they would connect me with a live tech after i filled out the form which was a pay wall.  Asus is receiving 0 stars for their support service. I took it to Office Max where they very kindly tried to download the drivers several times, and they said that it seemed like a hardware problem, and offered the solution of hardwiring it to the router, which is workiung great, except I'm tied to the length of the cord to the router. Office Max staff get 5 stars. I carefully read Amazon's return policy and that said I could return it if it was "dead on arrival," but that if their technicians determined that it was not "dead on arrival" they would charge me 15% of the price. I give Amazon 0 stars for that. I would have given this 0 stars, but it did turn on.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 6, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this when my 4 yr old HP kept giving me fits. I hear people saying that this laptop is slow, yada, yada, yada. First, anyone who knows anything about computers knows Windows is a storage and power hog. They put a lot of unnecessary stuff that is guaranteed to bog down a computer. First thing we did was wipe the laptop and install Linux Mint. Linux is lighter and faster than Windows. So, speed has not been an issue for me. My hubby said this is the fastest and easiest he has ever gotten Linux installed and we have been using Linux for the better part of 20 years. The screen is bright and crystal clear. I am blind as a bat and this screen is easy to read without any glare. I have had it unplugged for 3 and a half hours now and the battery power is only down to the 50% mark. Your are getting a $350 laptop, not a $1500 gaming computer. This is great for anyone NOT using it for gaming. I use it for facebook, bills, tracking my mileage and of course, Amazon shopping. I love this laptop, especially at the price it is.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on February 23, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This was bought after quite some time researching my options. I was looking for an adequate beginners laptop, with moderate performance, decent screen quality on a 15.6" screen, good wifi connections, and overall ease of use for basic purposes.The processor seems to be more than adequate for basic computing, and light office work. With only 8GB of RAM my concern would be the overall lifespan as to the possibility of needing more in the future, and this being unupgradable due to it being soldered onto the main board.Storage is plenty, and with a USB-C port there is always the ability to backup to a portable SSD to free up space when needed. Overall I would recommend this laptop for anybody needing something to complete basic tasks like web browsing, email, and light office work with documents. In fact, this review was written on it, and I am pleasantly surprised at how my ability to type on a chicklet style keyboard has improved over the couple of months I've had it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently upgraded my old Acer Predator to the MSI Vector 16, hoping for a smoother, low-maintenance experience with updated tech. I don't play that many games, so I was looking for something solid that wouldn't give me constant headaches. Unfortunately, after just one day of using the MSI Vector 16, I started running into issues.The laptop would freeze within a minute of startup, then crash to a black screen. The only software I had uploaded was Brave Browser, Chrome, Webroot Anti-virus, Office365, Steam, World of Tanks, and Star Trek Fleet Command—it was clear that the laptop was not being overworked. The system should’ve been able to handle that easily.A quick Google search revealed that MSI has a history of similar issues with their laptops, which was a big red flag. I reached out to MSI support, but their AI-driven support system was unhelpful, only offering basic troubleshooting steps (like ensuring the power cord was plugged in). This was extremely frustrating since I purchased this laptop to avoid endless hours of troubleshooting.The entire experience was disappointing, and I quickly realized I purchased a laptop that would require endless hours of diagnosing and problem solving, leaving me little time to actually enjoy the games I do play. This was my first MSI laptop, and it will definitely be my last.If you’re considering purchasing the MSI Vector 16, I sincerely hope you have better luck than I did. For me, it was a huge letdown.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great performance, poor heat, noise, and usability
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: At the price point, I expect high level performance and cannot deny that. While it this laptop undeniably hits that standard, it falls short in a lot of usability and comfort features.My biggest complaint is that despite being a laptop. The design seems to assume that no one is actually going to use it in their lap, especially for gaming.The cord is a straight out cord that is awkward when using it in your lap. It’s definitely causing pressure on the power input on the laptop and I expect to have an issue at some point with that connections becoming lose due to the pressure.The laptop also gets incredibly hot and vents directly out the side of the unit. I don’t think I could hold my hand directly in front of the heat output for long due to the heat. I use it on a lap pad, so it’s not an issue for me, but I question whether one could comfortably use the machine when it’s running hot, such as playing a game or processing video.This high heat is despite extremely loud fans. This is one area I wish had listened to reviews. I was warned, but I still underestimated the noise level.There was also a lot of bloatware on the machine for coming from a smaller company. Was a pain to get Mcafee actually removed.Overall, the performance is great, but the usability falls short for me, especially the heat and the noise. My previous laptop was from a custom build company and lasted me a decade, a formidable tool to the end. Given the chance to re-purchase, I would spend more for another custom vs what I got out of the box from MSI.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a great deal for a fast reliable computer.  I will share the one thing that I had to work hard to configure.  The backlit keyboard (controlled by F4) ships with a factory timeout of 30 seconds.  I found this to be a hassle, especially as I tend to keep the laptop plugged in, and I feel like I need the backlit keyboard.  I did not know how to change the setting for this until I asked Copilot!  Then I learned that I had to use a BIOS setting to set the timeout to "never".  I could still turn it on/off, or set to various brightness levels with F4.  The instructions were: Using my HP 2023 17t Business Professional, how do I set the backlit keyboard to stay on all the time?To set the backlit keyboard on your HP 2023 17t Business Professional to stay on all the time, follow these steps:Restart your laptop and immediately press the F10 key repeatedly until the BIOS setup opens.Navigate to the Advanced tab using the arrow keys.Go to Built-in Device Options and press Enter.  The Enter key enables selection of item choices.Select Backlit Keyboard Timeout and press the spacebar to open the settings.Choose "Never" to keep the backlight on at all times.Thanks CoPilot!  I do like the keyboard, and the fingerprint reader!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the AORUS Master, and it honestly exceeded expectations not just for performance, but for how smooth the whole setup and daily use has been.Out of the box, setup was effortless. Windows 11 loaded quickly, and everything was ready to go without bloat or weird popups. I also appreciated how easy it was to find the manual and drivers directly on GIGABYTE’s support page, super clean and helpful for someone who likes to fine-tune things.The fans stay impressively quiet under most loads. When they do ramp up during heavier tasks, it's more of a soft whoosh than a distracting whine. The cooling system feels smart, temperature stays balanced without sounding like a jet engine.Internally, there’s plenty of room for upgrades. I added a second SSD easily thanks to the accessible slot layout. It’s well thought out for long-term use, which not all laptops in this price range can claim.Performance-wise, the RTX 5070 Ti holds its ground extremely well. Benchmarked it myself, and the GPU score was just under flagship levels—really impressive for a machine this thin. I don’t just use this for gaming; I’m doing productivity work, photo editing, and media management, and it handles everything with headroom to spare.Also love the gi-Mate software besides performance profiles, it lets me tune the lighting and vibe of the laptop depending on where I’m using it. At home, I’ve got it set to a calm white. At work, I mute everything with a darker setup. It’s subtle but makes it feel more personal and adaptable.Overall, if you’re looking for a laptop that’s quiet, clean, customizable, and powerful, this is a solid choice, and not just for gamers. It’s a great all-around machine with high-end components and none of the friction.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Powerful and Vibrant laptop perfect for light gamers and everyday use
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Absolutely loving my GIGABYTE AORUS Master 16! The 240Hz OLED screen with that sharp 2560x1600 resolution makes gaming and streaming incredibly vivid and smooth. The RTX 5070 Ti handles everything I throw at it — from AAA games to creative work — without breaking a sweat. The Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX keeps things snappy, and 32GB DDR5 RAM means no lag even with multiple apps open. Plus, the 1TB SSD gives me plenty of space and lightning-fast load times. Windows 11 runs flawlessly. Overall, a powerhouse laptop that feels premium and delivers top-tier performance. I highly recommend it, and will recommend it to a friend.As a casual gamer who also uses the laptop for everyday tasks, I’m really impressed with how smooth everything runs. The display is a real standout — colors are vibrant and the high refresh rate makes even simple games feel fluid and responsive. It’s not just for heavy-duty gaming; watching movies and browsing feel way better on this screen compared to my old laptop. The keyboard is comfortable for long sessions, and the overall build feels sturdy but not too bulky, which is great for carrying around.Performance-wise, it handles light gaming and multitasking effortlessly. I can easily switch between streaming, web browsing, and gaming without any slowdown. The battery life isn’t bad either, considering the power inside, so I don’t feel tied down to a charger all the time. If you’re looking for a laptop that balances strong gaming capabilities with everyday use without going overboard, this GIGABYTE AORUS Master 16 hits the sweet spot.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked this up mainly for work, some creative projects, and light multitasking, but I have to say, it’s surprisingly overpowered in the best way.The Intel Ultra 9 chip in here is no joke. Everything opens instantly, and even under heavy multitasks (video calls, editing, running multiple tabs and programs), it doesn’t slow down. The RTX 5070 Ti adds a level of headroom I wasn’t expecting. I didn’t buy this just to push graphics, but it’s nice to know it can handle whatever I throw at it with zero stutter.What really stands out is the OLED display. It’s sharp, smooth, and just looks incredible. The 240Hz refresh rate makes everyday use feel noticeably snappier, even just scrolling or moving windows around. Colors are deep and rich, and it’s easy on the eyes for long hours.Design-wise, it’s got that clean, premium look with a little RGB personality—not flashy, but not boring either. It feels solid, not plastic-y, and the cooling doesn’t scream at you when things heat up.If you want a machine that looks good, feels premium, and performs beyond expectations, this one checks all the boxes.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: 5-star review! This 15.6 inch Gaming laptop i5 has been an absolute pleasure to use. The screen is sharp and detailed with excellent color reproduction on the IPS panel — perfect for watching videos or getting work done comfortably. The 180° hinge makes it super easy to share the screen with others. Performance is strong thanks to the i5 processor (up to 3.60GHz), 16GB RAM, and 512GB SSD. Multitasking feels smooth with tons of browser tabs and Office apps open, and even light gaming like League of Legends runs nicely without lag. The backlit keyboard is comfortable for typing at night, and the trackpad is precise and responsive. The laptop is slim and portable, making it ideal for students and professionals on the go. Cooling is well-managed — it stays cool during long sessions and the fan stays quiet. Battery life easily lasts a full day of studying, working, and entertainment.What impresses me most is the value. At just over $300, this configuration far outperforms other laptops in the same price range. After using it for nearly two weeks, it has been completely stable with no lag or issues. It feels like a big upgrade from my old laptop — productivity has improved noticeably. The packaging was nice, shipping was fast, and unboxing was a pleasant surprise. It comes with Windows 11 Pro pre-installed (secure and user-friendly) and has plenty of storage. Whether for daily office work, online classes, or casual gaming, this laptop handles everything excellently. If you’re looking for a reliable, well-rounded laptop on a budget, this one is definitely worth it. Highly recommended — full 5 stars

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Just bought this 15.6 inch Gaming Laptop for my upcoming month-long trip cuz I just need one that could handle some simple typing and browsing work because my old one does not update system anymore. After using it for a bit to test out before my trip, I'm happy with the purchase.The display is nice and just what i needed. Full HD screen is bright, clear, and comfortable for watching movies, browsing the web, and getting work done. Keyboard feels nice to type on, but no the backlit keys. It is ok since it really dosent matter that much to me. It also feels sturdy enough to travel with.Performance is better than I expected. Windows starts up quickly, programs open fast, and multitasking has been smooth. I usually have several browser tabs open along with browsers, music streaming, and slacks and everything runs without noticeable slowdowns.Tested the gaming part. As a budget version 15.6 inch Gaming Laptop, it handles casual gaming well. I don't expect it to replace a top build gaming desktop, but it's more than capable of running WOW and discord. The fans become noticeable under heavier using, but temperatures have stayed reasonable.Good thing I like is the variety of ports, making it easy to connect a mouse, external monitor, or other accessories without carrying a bunch of adapters. Battery life is pretty good enough for everyday tasks, though I still bring the charger when I know I'll be using it for extended periods.Overall, I think this laptop is excellent value for the price. It has the performance I need for work, enough power for casual gaming, and a screen with multipal settngs that's enjoyable for streaming and everyday use. For anyone looking for an affordable laptop, especially if you're planning to travel like I am, I think it's a solid choice.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Big, basic laptop. Did I say it was big?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Okay, so normally not a big believer in brand new, basic laptops. Like cars, I would prefer to buy a higher spec laptop that is a few years old for the same amount of money. However, when this came up on Prime Day as a flash sale for Prime members, I threw caution to the wind and recklessly spent my hard earned money on something that inflation had not yet seem to hit!Unpacking: Packaged like a refurb. Generic cardboard box with plastic wrapped laptop in foam holders, the AC adapter and two pieces of written documentation. That's it. No pretty outer box with all the specs, fancy pictures of even color. Though it looked like a refurb package, unit was in fact brand new. They didn't waste money on fancy packaging, which let's be honest, you don't need anyway.First Impressions: This thing is BIG. A 17" screen with 3/4" bezels on all sides is hard to imagine until you are holding it. Small, svelte and built for the road warrior this thing is not!Build quality: Okay, here is where the budget starts to shine through. The entire case looks like beautiful brushed aluminum...until you feel it. There is no mistaking this, it is the thinnest plastic that would hold the finish and provide a wet noodles worth of structural integrity. There is greater than expected flex to the chassis, the joints where the plastic panels meet feels like an old "snap tite" model and you just know that scratches and wear are going to be apparent in short order. I am now searching for a case, if they even make them for this as it appears to be a new model. This is a laptop that will feel more at home being a desktop replacement than your sidekick on roadtrips.Ports/Access: The box says seven ports, which is par for the course, but the composition of them again points to a budget price point. Standard USB, check. HDMI, check. Card reader, check. USB-C, nope. Separate headphone and microphone jacks, nope. And oh my, when was the last time you saw a wired ethernet port with the expandable "jaw" that opens to allow that massive plug? That is going back to pre wi-fi days. A USB-C and separate jacks for mic and audio would have been welcome in lieu of that wired ethernet jack. Again, though, this is a budget laptop and I will not fault the omissions at this price point. On that note, when I opened the laptop, I was pleasantly surprised by what appeared to be a fingerprint reader above the ESC key! Upon further examination, the "reader" turned out to be the physical power button and the only thing it will do with your finger is cycle up and down to turn the pc on and off. Also, in today's age of USB-C options, it would have been nice to see the AC port use the USB-C interface instead of the proprietary "blue tip" adapter that HP has been using for generations now. I guess the good news is that if you have a blue tip or three laying around, you have plenty of spare adapters.Function: Windows 11 boots right up and for those uninitiated to it, looks eerily similar to Apple's OS series. The bottom task bar is now a "dock" and quick launch icons are centered in it now. With 4 GB of RAM, an 11th gen i3 processor and onboard video being handled by Intel (and sharing in that massive 4 GB system RAM) this is not your gaming laptop. In fact, you may or may not realize that for the cost of a good graphics card today, you could easily buy two or three laptops like this for the price of a good GPU. Stick with Hearts, Solitaire and Minesweeper and you will be fine. I do not game, my work is office production and work related so I doubt I will tax the GPU and be very happy with what I find.  Overall, the laptop feels quick as expected for ordinary tasks, web surfing and production apps.Sound: Like TV's, the speakers are there for the most basic sound you can tolerate. If audio quality above the intense sound of an angry hornet in a tin can is what you crave, grab your headphones or external speakers and rock on.Keyboard: As is common today, "chiclet" keys with separate number pad to the right. For all of the real estate this size laptop creates, anything less than full size keys would be criminal (and comical in appearance). The keys have a nice feel to them. They are not cherry switches, but they do have tactile "thumps" when typing and don't feel like you are typing on top of foam rubber. Something I have become very accustomed to and greatly miss is a lighted keyboard. Unless I just cannot figure out how to turn it on, which I doubt. Suspiciously, every function key has an alternate function (like brightness up/down, volume up/down, track skip, play, and even airplane mode) EXCEPT for f5 which has no alternate function whatsoever. This is the typical location for keyboard light so it appears to be MIA. Again, for the price, not going to complain, and given that this is more a desktop replacement than a road warrior, it should not impact most users anyway.Noise: You can always tell an older laptop by the amount of time the fans kick up in speed when using it. For most newer laptops, rarely do you hear the fans spool up as the hardware can handle most standard tasks. The older the hardware gets, the more it gets tasked by updated apps and requirements, the more the fans spool up to accommodate the higher energy draw and load. I have yet to hear anything but a whisper from this laptop.Screen: No, it is not a touch screen. Yes, the panel exhibits a lot of variation when viewed from any angle other than directly looking at it. I would say the direct zone is about 45 degrees total from left to right before you get very noticeable color and brightness variations. If more than one person is viewing (or you let your kids use it in the car) it is best used by at most, two people sitting very close.Wrap Up: As with most anything in life, it is a balance of cost vs benefit. As I sit on this laptop and do this review, it is clear to me what HP focused on (and what they purposely left out) to provide a laptop at this price point. As a desktop replacement (complete with physical ethernet jack), this unit excels at a large display, a decently tactile keyboard, plenty of ports for common use, and sufficient hardware to meet the expectations of the production/surfing/simple web based gaming crowd. It will also please the occasional trip to the back porch for morning coffee while perusing your favorite blog. But start to travel a lot with this, putting it through the torture of soft sided cases, airport screeners or even just riding shotgun to and from work on a regular basis, it appears the chassis will quickly fall behind the performance of smaller display units or units made from actual brushed metal.I have another HP with a touch screen, metal case, double the memory and double the capacity SSD in it. If I factor price out of the equation, this laptop is less than satisfying. If I factor in the price and realize that the laptop I am comparing this one to is FOUR TIMES times more expensive, I am quite happy with the serviceability and performance of this! As with most things in life, you get what you pay for, and this is no exception.

Take your 15.6-inch laptop wherever you go and see more of your entertainment on an HD, micro-edge display (1). Not only do your games and movies look better, but with the AMD Radeon™ Graphics card, everything you do gets a performance boost (2). productPageReviews.reviewTitle: responsive, quick. Good machine for most needs, see data sheet link for details
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Not sure why anyone thought this is a touchscreen. Nowhere does it mention it. Take a look under "Product Guides and Documents", which you can find just above the review section. There you will see is a highlighted link to the "SPECIFICATION SHEET (PDF)". Click on that, and it will tell you even more detail about this machine than what is already outlined in the product description. And because of that, I wont rehash all what this has. But look for that link so you can decide if it has what you need!!!For those saying that this does not have a finger print ID? YES IT DOES. Search for it in your settings. IT IS A SETTING that you must set up. Hit the magnifying glass icon, then type in "fingerprint sign-in". Follow instructions. Can also set for using a PIN, which I do.Overall, it is a good basic laptop. Enough memory to load some photos and videos, plenty of processing power for a lot of basic uses: watching video, email, internet browsing, low end games. Likely good for most school needs, and some office needs. I haven't pushed it to the max because my needs are fairly low end. I have a separate high end desktop for true gaming needs, and for mega storage. Cant blame a machine for not doing what you want if you dont know anything about it to start. Learn what 8 gb ram is and what 512 gb ssd can do for you, and know what your needs are. Work up, or down from there. This seemed to be the sweet spot for my casual needs.It runs smoothly, quietly, and cool. Battery lasts a long while, which is nice for on the go use. Your experience may vary. Depends on what you are doing, your settings, etc.Very responsive, though like I said I havent put it through the paces.Even Microsoft Edge is blazing quick and easy to use. I had it on my last laptop (half the memory and processing) and it was all I could run. I figured I would be switching to firefox, but I keep using Edge without issue.Responsive touchpad, though since I prefer using a mouse I turned off the touchpad.Optional backlit keyboard. Can turn on or off, or up at any time with press of buttonQuickly boots up, good instant connectivitySpeakers are fine. Crisp. They are perfectly good, and offer some mild range. They dont make my ears bleed when I watch a music video.ONLY thing I have experienced that has been bothersome is that sometimes my "m" key doesnt register. I will be typing along, and the letter m did not actually type. However, it is hit and miss, and it might be a matter of how I am sitting or something. I havent had the experience while writing this review. Unless you notice missing m's that I didnt.I' pleased. So far so good. I am giving it 5 stars (4.5 if we could do half ratings), and am giving it that for the CLASS of laptop, and that it is what the product description says it is. Minor annoyances regarding anti virus, updates, microsoft stuff is typical across computers. All in all, it is what I expected, nothing negative that I can think of, and if I experience anything else worth sharing--good, bad, or otherwise-- I will do so. I keep up with my reviews. I am an avid reviewer and aim to be helpful as much as possible.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I can't believe people are giving this five star reviews. Buying this laptop was a complete regret. The only thing nice about it is the OLED screen, which is fabulous. Seriously amazing panel, HDR500 certified. However, everything else is terrible!!!!11!11one1Here's a rundown of all the major flaws:-No display port to actually use the 5070ti and the display port over usb-c is WILDLY unstable. You basically have to disconnect and reconnect your monitor after EVERY boot if you want to do anything above 144hz refresh rate or high resolutions with many monitors.-Takes forever to boot, every single time. The BIOS boot phase is nuts long before it even starts booting windows.-Major problem with USB suspend states and thunderbolt that updates still haven't fixed in 2026.-Battery life is TERRIBLE. Less than 2 hours just web browsing with nothing else running.-Randomly crashes all the time, regardless of drivers and bios firmware updates. Start a game and 10% chance it just randomly locks up completely and eventually reboots itself.-Two USB-C ports, and you can't even use both if you use more than one monitor.-Uses a TON of power all the time if you use external monitors because you cannot power down the 5070ti card. Even at idle, she chews 110w just chilling because HDMI and DP Alt Mode over USB-C are designed to go through the Nvidia card.-Screen runs all the time unless you disconnect it in windows because there's no lid closed sensor, or at least one that works. Power button also on the keyboard so you can't use this "docked" anyway.Many of these issues are hardware designs you won't find on other laptop designs and these cannot be fixed with software. If I could return this laptop, I absolutely would. It's not worth the nightmare.Don't take my word for it either. Do a quick websearch for Acer Refurbished and you'll find Acer literally selling thousands and thousands of these because the return and failure rate is so high.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Extremely Slow, Clunky, Cheaply Made, Cheap Plastic
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was so excited about purchasing this small capacity laptop for just my writing. As simply as that. Nothing more.  Well... it couldn't even handle that. I started it up and it took 10 tries for it to be able to connect to my WiFi. After it finally did, it experienced such slow hangups uploading software and loading internet pages that I was not even able to install chrome. I would type something in the browser window and the text wouldn't start showing up until 5-6 seconds later. It would blank/freeze screen while trying to load Edge. It wouldn't even load up the installed Word application.  I tried over several hours to get this thing to just let me pull up my Drive page so I could see how it does with my typing and it was so slow that I just gave up.  No computer should be this slow or be this difficult to update. It's very cute and if it weren't such a bad performer, I'd actually ignore that it's made of very cheap plastic and I really had to lay on the touchpad to get it to click in a very specific spot. I'd have been okay with that since typing doesn't really take much touchpad use unless editing and I would have been okay with it.  But.. because I couldn't even get past trying to load up a page, I was done.  Not worth the hassle. Returned it next day.  Please don't bother buying this - you're taking the risk of having to fuss around with it for hours to no avail. Someone reviewed that this was good for older folks - I don't think it is. It's not good for anyone. Just a horrible, outdated, lagging, cheaply made useless device. On to my search for a different laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This little PC is a great value
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This HP laptop is lightweight, so perfect for carrying from room to room at home and to meetings, too.  Have had no issues; no worries about missing a huge storage drive either, since I can connect to my backup drive anytime needed or use the cloud.  Not having DVD read/write is no big deal because I have that ability on my desktop, and never use it anyway! This has a flash card reader, 2 USBs, 1 C and an HDMI connection.  What else do I need?  This is not a gaming laptop or an accountant's dream (no 10-key) and, although it is not a touchscreen, it is perfect for everyday use at home and for light office work.  The case is plastic and feels a little cheap, but who cares?  It is dark blue and textured so never shows fingerprints or dirt.  Sure, I would take a higher end model if I didn't have to pay for it, but this meets my needs and my expectations. I'm perfectly happy with this item.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good value, but watch for damage and who you buy from!Good value, but watch for damage and who you buy from!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Good value. I purchased this model: (HP 255 G10 Laptop, Ryzen 3 7330U, 15.6", 16GB RAM, 1TB SSD with Windows 11 Pro) from the seller Chromebook Prosale via Amazon for $399 in December of 2024.I had to return the first one because it had a RAM error. Every other time I started it, the Caps Lock LED would blink (3 long and two short). According to the documentation, that meant a RAM issue. Might have just needed a cleaning or the RAM was installed improperly. (more on that later.) I'll never know because I didn't want to void the warranty. So I sent it back and the seller promptly sent a new one. No errors on that one. YAY!Booted it up and it indeed had no errors, recognized all hardware, and had Windows 11 Pro installed. All good. Pretty quick. WiFi has typical range. There are two USB ports, one HDMI port, and one 1/8" audio jack. Battery holds a charge like a champ. No security port. However, I'm pretty satisfied with this laptop.Being satisfied, I then voided the warranty and opened the system to take a look. (I don't recommend this for the casual user because, though I'm not sure, I think it will void your warranty - if they find out that is!)Now the interesting part:TLDR: Be careful when buying from third-party sellers. You might save money, but you never know where the laptop has been or whose grubby paws were inside it!See attached image of the RAM. Note that only one stick is covered with a sticker. This leads me to believe that HP built this laptop with 8 GB of RAM (1 stick) originally. I can't prove it, but I think that the seller (or another intermediary) installed the 2nd stick of RAM to bring it up to 16 GB. Three clues led me to this deduction (which is guesswork): 1 - the lack of a sticker. That's weak sauce, and HP QA would probably not let that pass before leaving the manufacturer. 2. One of the panel's front corners was slightly lifted off two of the clips, as if the person who closed the panel (after installing the RAM) didn't finish the job properly. Made it easier for me to pop the panel though! 3. The first laptop I received had that RAM issue I mentioned. That would probably not pass QA at an HP manufacturing plant either. Standard procedure is to have a system booted at least three times.Am I happy with my assumption? No. But I'll deal with it after inspecting the RAM installed and comparing it with the first 8 GB stick. The laptop looks clean and I inspected Windows 11 as well for any "weirdness" or inappropriate programs.That said, would I purchase this again or recommend it. Only if a person's sole criteria for buying was price. Generally, I recommend buying laptops from the manufacturer directly.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Matryoshka Doll Packaging, But A Trojan Horse InsideMatryoshka Doll Packaging, But A Trojan Horse Inside
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: ​The packaging was top-tier. It arrived incredibly fast, safely and securely packed inside an Amazon box, which contained an MSI box, which contained another box. It was like unboxing a high-tech Matryoshka doll. I also appreciated that the driver required a secure delivery code, ensuring the package actually made it into the right hands.​Unfortunately, that’s where the good news ends.​Once I opened the final doll, the unit I received was deeply problematic from day one. The display suffered from severe, constant graphics glitching right out of the box. Even more alarming, upon closer inspection, I noticed highly suspicious battery swelling that was actively pushing against the chassis.​Because of these blatant hardware and safety defects, this unit had to go straight back. Leaving a buyer stuck dealing with a hazardous, defective device like this with absolutely no resolution makes for an incredibly exhausting experience. I’ve attached photographic evidence clearly showing the screen failures and the battery hazard so others know what to look out for.​Given the hardware lottery and the safety risk of a swollen battery, I can't recommend risking your money on this specific unit. Look elsewhere to avoid weeks-long headaches.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Can't even play World of Warcraft.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really was looking forward to this laptop, but very disappointed in how it handles games.  The first game I downloaded was WoW, and I can't even play it, the graphics rip, tear, and hitch constantly, and even worse if I use the HDMI to plug in a big monitor, plus the memory usage when just running WoW alone would go up to 80%, there is no reason it should be doing that, unless it's all the bloat ware running in the background, which I tried to get rid of most of it.  As far as the Noise Level that was not an issue, and I do like the build, the design allows breathing room so it doesn't overheat, which is very important in a gaming laptop.I haven't really got a chance to see how well the battery life is, because I've spent the majority of my time just trying to get WoW to run without graphic issues, and  because of the graphic issues I am returning it.  Here is the deal, I am technical, and I work on computers for a living, but when I buy a computer, that claims to run games with ease, that is what I expect!  I shouldn't have to do a ton of stuff to just play a simple game like World of Warcraft, this should work out of the box without tweaking anything.  I am giving this a 3 star because I do love the case design, that is an A+, if it weren't for that it would get a 1 star.

Competitive advantage: Compete faster with NVIDIA Reflex 2 technology featuring Frame Warp, which further reduces latency based on the game’s latest mouse input.

items.title: Comfort focused design
items.text: Intentionally designed for comfortable, everyday use. Alienware 16 Aurora’s streamlined design offers advanced thermal support without the need for a rear thermal shelf. The laptop’s smaller profile makes it an easy fit into bags and backpacks for on-the-go performance.

items.title: Easy to carry. Hard to put down.
items.text: Premium build: Alienware 16 Aurora is designed with premium materials, such as an anodized aluminum lid featuring an iridescent Alienware logo and magnesium alloy interior frame.

items.title: Fluid contours
items.text: Soft, smooth contours make the laptop more comfortable to hold, complimented by a stunning new colorway Interstellar Indigo with a satin finish.

items.title: Comfort ensured
items.text: Opening and closing your laptop lid just got easier thanks to an angled front edge. Plus, a gently pillowed palm rest ensures comfort during any gaming session.

items.title: Ready for tomorrow
items.text:
With ample storage and memory, Aurora is built to game and multitask today and beyond. This laptop features two upgradeable PCIe Gen 4 SSD slots and two user-upgradeable DDR5 SO-DIMM memory slots. 
Purchase model configurations will vary. Subject to third party purchase of additional storage. SSDs are user-replaceable for up to 2TB of total SSD storage. It's recommended to add a bracket and thermal pad when you add 2230 SSD to upgrade your storage capacity.

Integrated camera
HD camera with integrated dual array microphone.

Crystal-clear 16” display
16:10 WQXGA 120Hz panel with 300 nits, sRGB 100% with ComfortView Plus low blue light technology.

Faster connectivity
Wi-Fi 7 enabled and RJ-45 Ethernet port. Take advantage of fast transfer speeds, reduced latency and increased throughput for smoother gaming and multitasking.

Precision keyboard
A white-backlit keyboard with a dedicated AI key and full numpad.

Audio essentials
Get immersed with two 2W speakers with Dolby Audio.

items.title: Precision cooling for maximum efficiency
items.text:
The new Cryo-Chamber design optimizes airflow, cooling and performance. 
Intentional airflow: Air is strategically pulled in above the keyboard and in the Cryo-Chamber, and out four exhaust vents on the sides. 
Quiet and cool: Expertly designed fans keep the system running smoothly and quietly. 
Built to last: Efficient thermal design protects internal components and extends the life of the system.

items.title: Advanced thermals for extended play
items.text: Our advanced cooling technology, Alienware Cryo-tech, is designed to maintain system stability even during the most demanding sessions.

items.title: Dual fans
items.text:
Two fans with ultra-thin blades pull cool air in from the top and bottom; exhaust hot air out 4 vents to help enable higher performance. 
Copper heat pipes: Three copper heat pipes dissipate heat from the CPU and GPU ensuring seamless gaming.

items.title: Blend into any environment
items.text:
Activate Stealth Mode with F7 to switch performance to Quiet Mode for a more subtle, covert experience. 
Quiet mode lowers noise produced by your system's cooling fans when possible. While your computer's performance might be slightly impacted, this option may also reduce both CPU and GPU power consumptions.

items.title: Total command
items.text:
Convenient presets: Maximize your gameplay with performance presets for the power you need, no matter what you're doing. 
Performance overlay: Manage and see CPU, GPU, memory and thermals stats without exiting the game. 
AlienFX: Customize your setup with lighting settings that extend to all your Alienware accessories, as well as key binds and calibration. 
AlienVision: Toggle external Alienware monitor hardware-based overlays on/off to help you focus on the targets at hand.

items.title: Balanced power
items.text:
The perfect balance of performance and portability in a stunning chassis. Ready to run your favorite games seamlessly with up to 115W Total Performance Power. 
Up to 115W: Total Performance Power is the combined maximum of TGP and TDP, enhancing overall performance across all you do. 
Up to 70W: Total Graphics Power means higher GPU performance with more realistic gameplay. 
Up to 45W: CPU Thermal Design Power means full power devoted towards processing tasks in real-time.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Be sure to inspect the laptop, including components. Terrible service from all companies involved.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The laptops in this Alienware x16 series are all monsters (or aliens, whatever lol), but be sure to do some digging to see if you got what you paid for.[MY SETUP]I hooked it up to a 34-inch ultrawide monitor (3440x1440), the RTX 4080, Ultra 9 185H CPU, and 32GB RAM play almost every game at max settings with smooth FPS. Stuff like 3D modeling and photo-editing is a breeze too.I like the keyboard, this one has the normal one, not the mechanical one. But I like it better because it's quiet and it's comfortable to type on.Also note it has Windows 11, if you don't want to make an online account just to use your computer, you have to use Terminal to reactivate the Local Account button during the setup stage. Then it's just a matter of removing bloatware with the usual utilities out there.[BE SURE TO INSPECT THE LAPTOP YOU GET, INCLUDING THE HARDWARE!]Amazon says professionals inspect every laptop they have for resale, but...I don't know. Here are the problems I found:-The screen is listed as the 240Hz version, but the one received is 165Hz. It also clearly has a patch of dead pixels in the corner.-There were screws loose from the bottom and the shell wasn't assembled correctly after "inspection".-The exhaust fins had dings in them because the big power adapter was just rattling around in the box. Ugh. That's going to affect cooling.-The hard drive and CPU are fine, so is the RAM because it's soldered to the motherboard. The battery health seems good, though this is something you'll keep plugged in all the time most likely.-The listing says you get a free year of Alienware Premium Support with this laptop, but you don't. I checked the service tag with Dell and it only has Basic Support. (Don't share your service tag with anyone but offical Dell support.) Amazon customer service said it came with 3 years of Asurion insurance, also not true. I was not compensated for either of these false/missing things.[UPDATE]Having used it for a while now, seems like Alienware laptops have driver issues and software you can't get rid of.-Often the laptop won't recognize that anything is plugged into the headphone jack, it has to be restarted to force it to work.-Killer Suite supposedly helps "manage your internet" but all it does is screw things up and refuses to be uninstalled unless you buy your own wifi card.-Windows Updates are also borked, the laptop keeps asking to restart to install "Intel Network Platform Performance" or whatever nonsense because it doesn't understand it's already updated. What a pain in the bum.-I contacted Dell Alienware Support and they haven't responded in over a week. I'm never buying a Dell again.So anyway, if you paid almost $2000 for this used laptop, go ahead and be angry, that's a poor value. In the condition I got it, it has like $600 worth of mistakes, that's not something you should overlook.
