productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Just an excellent laptop that's a beast of a gaming rig, but won't annihilate your bank account.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have a an older MSI laptop I got for a really good price several years ago, a GL65 Leopard with a 10th gen Core i7 and the RTX2070 Super. The construction was on the cheaper end of things, and that 10th gen i7 ran darn near hot as the sun. But with some tweaks using Throttlestop, I got the temps under control and it ended up being a fantastic mobile gaming rig. That full tilt 2070 Super was one heck of a GPU for gaming. But it was more on the budget end of their product line and it was obvious. Still, I enjoyed using it a great deal. It wasn't as nice looking or feeling as the Asus laptops I usually bought. But it ripped along nicely when gaming. In late 2024, they had a great deal on an Asus TuF laptop with a Ryzen 9 7940HX and a RTX4070 GPU, so I handed the Leopard off to my son and picked up the Asus. Fantastic laptop as well, but the mobile RTX4070 left a lot to be desired.I was perfectly happy with that until I came across this laptop in December 2025. It was on sale for really good price, and with what I knew of the new mobile RTX5070ti, I went for it. The Vector series are more towards the upper end of their line, and it shows. This thing is kind of a beast when it comes to gaming. The 5070ti mobile with 12GB of GDDR7 on a 192 bit pipeline absolutely crushes the RTX4070 mobile, hands down. I wasn't sure about going back to an Intel processor, especially after using the TuF and its Ryzen 9. And I know the Series 2 chips had issues early on, but it has proven itself to be extremely capable. I did some tweaking to the to the clock curve to help it run a bit cooler, but it ran quite well even in its factory configuration. As for what MSI did with this laptop, it's really a solid rig all around. The laptop's chassis is really nice and solid feeling. The hinges looked as though they might be a bit spindly, but they've also proven themselves to be solid. The keyboard is great, the QHD+ screen is fast, bright, and has a quite wide viewing angle. The cooling solution is very capable, but does get fairly loud when the laptop is running flat out. But I have heard louder rigs and it doesn't bother me much as I almost always use headphones if I'm gaming. The audio solution in the Vector is actually not half bad, especially for a laptop. But it is still laptop, and laptops in general aren't exactly known for their audio quality. But it's perfectly fine for general use, and significantly better than a lot of laptops I've had in the past. The Vector is well loaded with ports having 2.5 G LAN and a full size HDMI 2.1 port on the rear, 2x USB3.2Gen2 ports and a 3.5mm audio jack on the right side, 2x Thunderbolt 5 ports and an SD 7.0 port on the left side. It's a very clean design overall with plenty of ventilation and it's quite easy to access the interior to install RAM, SSDs, or to swap out your WiFi module. Speaking of WiFi, it comes with Intel's Killer WiFi 7 BE1750 for which I have absolutely no complaints. The touchpad is decently large and pretty responsive, but I'm not a big fan of touchpanels, so I almost always have a mouse at hand except when space is too tight to use one. The screen camera is ok, and the microphone setup works decently enough, but nothing to write home about. It does have a manual shutter to block the camera. And of course, it does come with the typical load of bloatware that infests all laptops and prebuilt desktops these days, but if you're comfortable doing it, you can always blow out the system and run a "clean" installation of Win11(Well, as clean as Win11 gets anyway, which isn't saying much.) or your preferred Linux build. I've chosen to stick with Win11 for the time being, but have already uprooted all the Microsoft AI garbage through the use of one of the many methods available online. Doing so does help free up a good bit of resources that MS's AI junk takes up.But overall, I really don't have any major complaints with the Vector. It's just a really good gaming laptop that's well built and comes in at a price that won't destroy your bank account. It's not a top of the line build as far as laptops go, but it also doesn't have that top end price. It does everything it needs to do, and does it really well. It's not as nice as something with a full metal chassis, mechanical keys, and an OLED panel. It has some plastic chassis bits, but still feels plenty solid. It has a chiclet keyboard that's about as good as it gets for chiclet keys. It has a very fast and excellent LCD panel. In my opinion, that's a perfectly acceptable tradeoff to take for an incredibly powerful mobile gaming rig that's probably a third the cost you'd be looking at in anything else with the Vector's specs. Maybe less. It's a bit hard to compare these days with DDR5 and storage prices having gone completely off the rocker like they are now. But if you're looking for a beast of a rig, you'd do quite well to consider one of these.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Exactly what I was looking for....
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So while the price of a little over 1,400 was a little on the cheaper side for a 40 series gaming laptop (which is what I was looking for) I was a bit hesitant because going through the store page it left some things not mentioned that made me question if I could trust this seller for such a big ticket purchase.Add that there were no reviews at the time and that just increased my anxiety.But I pulled the trigger and I am glad I did.I have been putting it through its paces for about a week now and love the performance bump I get from my previous 3060 laptop.So a few things that you may be interested in.First the display runs up to 165hz which isn't mentioned in the above page....this is more then I was willing to settle for and was happy to see it was above 120hz.It does have a second ssd slot for expansion which I added my 2tb from my old laptop....its a 2 minute install, very easy.Comes with a 4070 and a 14650hx cpu as advertised.Runs fantastic and Lenovo thankfully lets you press the gpu/cpu if your willing to do so right in there own program which lets you overclock if you want.The fan noise is perfectly in range when it is full blast and the laptop stays cool for a gaming laptop.Havent had an throttling or any issue with the way its designed.The laptop came double boxed so its not screaming to have someone walk off with it on your porch and the laptop box has an armory of foam securing and protecting it....I'm not one not to complain when I think something I purchase falls short....but for the life of me I simply haven't had a single negative issue with this laptop as of now....everything gets a checkmark and Im not new to gaming laptops....I know in general what is considered a pro or con.I suppose if you want an aluminum chasses like my older msi stealth that could be considered a con....but that one cost me $600 more and the hard plastic chasses on this is thick and durable....the inside is what counts and this laptop does gaming justice.I have no hesitation recommending it to anyone who wants a middle top of the line current series gaming laptop....this is a great choice!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 7, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I’m extremely happy with this productI’m extremely happy with this product
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was looking for a good offer in a gaming laptop this last prime and I found this one for an incredible price to be honest. The laptop looks beautiful, I love the color, the details, the screen size, also the keyboard looks beautiful with the RGB and it is really soft when you type. So basically, if you’re are looking for a top gaming laptop, I really doubt you’re gonna find something better for this price, for me it’s an absolute YES, you’re not gonna regret.
